label: Science & Mathematics

Question: why moon cannot be used as a satellite?
Answer: Well the moons rotation is not a problem because it is tidally locked with the earth. It always has the same face pointing towards to earth.

There are a few reasons why it isn't practical to use it as a satellite. As has been mentioned above it is expensive to get there, and it is far enough away to have a significant delay in transmission.

Apart from that, there is another reason. When we deploy satellites we generally want to have extremely precise orbits. We may want a geostationary orbit, so the satellite is always in the same position relative to the earth, or we may want a satellite that covers the whole earth at one time or another. With the moon we have absolutely no control over its orbit, so unless you're lucky enough to have it in exactly the right orbit for you (highly unlikely), it's pretty useless.

Title: Whats the probability of having at least 3 girls in a family of six children?
Question: My genetics teacher said the answer should be out of 64, because there are 64 different family combinations.  Any help with figuring out this question would be great.
Answer: each child can be a male or a female 
therefore the total no of events possible is 2^6=64

the question says that you should have atleast 3 girls 
i.e there can be three, four ,five or all six girls .

the number of ways of choosing 3,4,5,6 girls from 6 children is the sum
6C3 + 6C4 + 6C5 + 6C6 (here C stands for combinations )

i,e

(6*5*4)/(3*2*1) + (6*5*4*3)/(4*3*2*1) + (6*5*4*3*2)/(5*4*3*2*1) + 1
this reduces to 
20+15+6+1
=42

therefore the probability is 
42/64

Title: Polarization question?
Question: Unpolarized light passes through two polarizers in turn with polarization axes at 42° to each other. What is the fraction of the incident light intensity that is transmitted?
Answer: Assuming ideal polarizers, the first one passes 50% of the light, and the second one passes (cos(42°))^2 of that, so the total light intensity transmitted is:

(0.5) * (cos(42°))^2 = 0.276132...

or about 27.6% of the incident light intensity.

Title: How can the rationale for punishment specifically retribution seen as social cohesion?.?
Question: retribution is generally seemed to socially exclusive because it seems to deny someone's rights thereby excluding that indivdiual from society, however i need to argue that it is, so my question is that is there anyway retribution can be seen as socially cohesive?.
Answer: Wow, that's tough.  Is your assignment to argue that retribution is socially cohesive, or did you come up with this yourself?

This is what I can think of:

Retributive justice is based on the idea that criminals should be punished for undermining social "harmony" or "balance."  Therefore, we can't dole out retributive punishment before we first have a definition of what is social harmony or balance.  Social harmony and balance can be defined through laws, custom, or religion.  The PROCESS of defining social harmony and balance is socailly cohesive because, to some extent, we must generally agree on what the definition of social order is.  In other words, the PROCESS of accepting and agreeing on laws/customs/religion is socially cohesive.

The rehabilitation theory of punishment is probably the most socially cohesive because it is based on rehabiliting the criminal so that he can successfully reenter society.

Title: what is a karat? is it a measure of weight? how does it relate to grams, or oz.?
Question: this is as it pertains to gems. A four karat gem is how much in grams , or onces?
Answer: Definition: The karat system is used to reveal the amount of pure gold found in an item.

    * 24 karat (24K) gold is pure gold.

    * 18 karat (18K) gold contains 18 parts gold and 6 parts another metal or metals, making it 75% gold.

    * 14 karat (14K) gold contains 14 parts gold and 10 parts another metal or metals, making it 58.3% gold.

    * 10 karat (10K) gold contains 10 parts gold and 14 parts another metal or metals, making it 41.7% gold. 10k gold is the minimum karat designation that can still be called gold in the US.

Common Misspellings: The term carat, spelled with a "c," refers to the weight of a gemstone.

Definition: A carat is a measure of weight used for gemstones, and is equal to 200 milligrams. Weights are given to the nearest 1/100th of a carat, an amount which is called a "point." For example, a .50 carat gemstone might also be called one-half carat or a 50-point stone.

Answer: To be perfectly honest with you, the best way to do boxing at home, is to not do boxing at home. There's all kinds of reasons for this, but I will give you only a couple. I'm writing to you about this with over 33 years of experience and many failed attempts of "Boxing at home"

   There's the little mistakes that you pick up while you're training at home, dropping your hand as you throw your jab, not shooting your jab straight out, not pivoting on your foot properly when throwing the left hook, stepping straight back with your head up in the air, cat-pawing when you start to get tired. These are the most common of mistakes that everyone starting out training at home does, maybe not all of them but definitely some of them.

  Then there's the fact that you're not around the gym atmosphere
the smell of a boxing gym. The subconscious telling you to push yourself harder than the guy hitting the bag next to you. The fact that your being watched by guys/girls who know what they're doing and you want to show that you belong. The fact that the noises that come from a gym give you a rush unlike anything you've ever experienced.

   The money you spend on a "Home Gym" will be a complete waste, how many times have you bought something you had to have and six months later you thought what a waste? Spend your money on a Gym membership or Gym dues, stay away from Health Clubs like Ballys, Golds Gym, World Gym and countless others who know absolutely nothing about boxing except Rocky's coming out on Christmas.

  I understand your position completely, to just stay in shape get yourself a freestanding bag, it's a great way to stay in shape. It's next to impossible to get into the shape you have to be in to actually compete at home, for all the above mentioned reasons and then some.

  Good luck.

Question: What causes a yeast infection and how do you stop it from itching so much??
Answer: Basically, a yeast infection is caused when there is a build up of yeast in the system. This happens a lot to people who have an excess of Candida Albicans in the system (caused by eating too much refined sugar and white flour and not enough whole foods, fruits and vegetables), and can also happen from a buildup of bacteria locally. If you wear the same underwear for too long, or wear a wet bathing suit for longer than half a day, it can happen quite easily. Some women get minor Yeast infections every month right before their period, and the period usually resolves the infection. They're normal, you just have to make sure you see a doctor if you get them TOO regularly, because this could mean you have an auntoimmune disorder you're unaware of. Also, you want to go to a doctor the first time you think you have one so he or she can make sure it's not something else; a lot of Sexually Transmited Infections can mimic Yeast Infections, as can Vaginitis and Bacterial Infections. It's best to check with your doctor, but if you already have and are looking for a good anti-itch remedy, put some plain yogurt on the itchy areas and the 'good' pro-biotic bacteria in the yogurt will fight the 'bad' bacteria, helping to soothe the itch and reinforce the good bacteria.

Answer: Here's a do/don't:  when smelling a chemical, don't just stick your nose over it, like you would smell something in everyday life.  Hold the test-tube, flask, etc, away from your face, and waft some of the fumes toward your nose with your hand.  Then, if it's not really nasty, you can smell some more in the normal way.

Another:  When inserting a glass tube into a cork or stopper, first be  sure you make the edges rounded by polishing it with a bunsen burner.  Then be sure to lubricate it.  Glycerine is normally used for that, though spit can be effective when the former isn't available.  If you don't do these things, the tube won't go in easily, and can break and jab you.  That happened to me when I was a kid.  It made a pretty bad gash in my finger.

For all you pyros out there ;) : Never grind an oxidizer and fuel together.  If you use the same mortar & pestle to grind the oxidizer and fuel, clean it thoroughly between grindings.

Title: do you agree that math should be illegal?
Question: i think it should only be used as a torture method in order to extract secrets from the enemy prisoners!!
Answer: Math is used all the time in the engineering sciences.  Many physical phenomena, including fluid flow, heat transport, and diffusion can be described by appropriate partial differential equations.  In order to solve these equations and make predictions, you need to be good at calculus.

If you limit yourself to addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, you would be stuck with linear models for everything.  This means that any more complicated relationship between two variables could not be modeled continuously, and you would never be able to extrapolate with any confidence.  Thus development of new technology would be strictly trial and error (and you wouldn't even have a good trial and error system without statistics).

Hang in there!  Get through that math.  You don't have to like it, but you will inevitably appreciate the developments that math has enabled.

christians and many different religions seem to always have evidence for their belief in god's existence. From this point of view they would not have faith, for faith is belief without evidence.

so, it seems that agnostics are the ones with faith, while the thesist (christians etc...) are the one without faith. maybe that explains the many problems with todays religions.
Answer: I think you may have your terms a little off.  

An agnostic is someone who feels that the belief in a diety cannot be proven therefore his or her own belief is one of ambivalence. They don't necessarily have faith, but they don't necessarily deny God's existence either.  They are simply saying they don't know.

Question: are chiropractors real doctors?
Answer: Doctors of Chiropractic receive extensive, demanding professional education on par with medical doctors (MDs) and osteopaths (DOs).
To receive the doctor of chiropractic degree, candidates must complete extensive undergraduate prerequisites and four years of graduate-level instruction and internship at an accredited chiropractic institution. Comprehensive knowledge of all systems of the body and diagnostic procedures enable the DC to thoroughly evaluate a patient, address disorders relating to the spine and determine the need for referral to another health care provider.

Doctors of Chiropractic are primary health care providers.
According to the Center for Studies in Health Policy, "The DC can provide all three levels of primary care interventions and therefore is a primary care provider, as are MDs and DOs. The doctor of chiropractic is a gatekeeper to the health care system and an independent practitioner who provides primary care services. The DC's office is a direct access portal of entry to the full scope of service."

Doctors of Chiropractic are licensed in all 50 states.
DCs have been licensed and recognized for many decades in all states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico.

Chiropractic is recognized by governmental health care programs.
Chiropractic is included in Medicare, Medicaid, Federal Employees Health Care Benefits Programs, Federal Workers' Compensation and all state workers' compensation programs. Chiropractic students are qualified to receive federal student loan assistance and DCs are authorized to be commissioned as health care officers in the U.S. Armed Forces.

The practice of chiropractic is based on sound scientific principles.
The existence of the nervous system as the primary control mechanism of the body is an undisputed scientific fact. Its relationship with the spine is the focus of the practice of chiropractic. The spine develops in utero to provide two primary functions: (1) allow for freedom of movement and (2) house and protect the spinal cord. When the vertebrae of the spine become misaligned through trauma or repetitive injury, two major consequences will result: (1) the range of motion becomes limited and (2) spinal nerves emerging from the spinal cord are compromised. DCs use the term "subluxation" to describe such disruptions. Interruption of nerve flow can eventually lead to pain, disability, and an overall decrease in the quality of life. Conversely, the removal of that interference has been shown to have significant, lasting health benefits. Through the adjustment of the subluxation, the doctor of chiropractic endeavors to restore normal nerve expression. The body is then able to respond appropriately to any imbalance in the system, thus relieving symptoms and restoring health.

Doctors of chiropractic provide effective, low-cost health care for a wide range of conditions.
Studies conducted according to the highest scientific standards and published by organizations not affiliated in any way with chiropractic institutions or associations continue to show the clinical appropriateness and effectiveness of chiropractic care. One of the most recent, funded by the Ontario Ministry of Health, stated emphatically that:

"On the evidence, particularly the most scientifically valid clinical studies, spinal manipulation applied by chiropractors is shown to be more effective than alternative treatments for low back pain...There would be highly significant cost savings if more management of low back pain was transferred from physician to chiropractors."

The doctor of chiropractic is an effective source of preventative and wellness care.

sentence:
Title: Neighbor keeps opening gates to my driveway saying it's her land and we cannot close the gates?
Question: My neighbor who is mentally ill is claiming that our driveway is part of her property.  We have been closing our gates for the last couple of weeks to keep her vicious dog out so that our grandchildren can play in the yard without fear of getting bitten.   The neighbor will come right behind us everytime we close the gate and open it back up yelling and cussing saying it's her land and we cannot close the gates.  What kind of action can I take against this woman?  I cannot sleepl, eat or have peace of mind for fear of her hurting me or my family.
Answer: First you really need to make sure that the gates are on your land and that both your Deed and hers do not contain any type of easement, right of ingress or egress, covenant blah blah that entitles her to do this.  Don't assume anything. You probably have your Deed in your files, and you can look at hers for free at the clerk or recorders office.  Many people are amazed to find that their Deed does have one of the above.  

Once you are certain she does not have this right, you can file a complaint in Municipal Court against her.  Chain and padlock the gate while you wait for your court date.  If she keeps it up after you go to court and win, you can probably have her arrested.  At the very least, the police will have to deal with her because you will have an order or decision.  If she gets herself arrested, and she is truly "mentally ill" as you say, there is a chance that she will be remanded for observation.

"We have called the police, 911 and the local dhhr and the humane society and NO ONE will do anything."   

Of course not. The police don't settle Deed issues, she hasn't done anything crazy enough for dhhr to get involved, and the dog hasn't been ruled vicious.  You are going about this all the wrong way, and all you are doing is frustrating yourself.  You are asking people to do things that are not in their power to do.

You need to first check the Deeds and proceed with a complaint filed in Municipal Court against her if you are truly in the right as per your Deeds. Anything less is just going to generate more frustration on your part.

Title: I need an approx. volume of a pond please.?
Question: I have a pond in my back yard about 50X18. It is usually 4-5ft deep and the banks are nothing extraordinary, no retaining walls etc. I would like to determine the volume of water for chemical treatment purposes. The formula would be even better. (you might have to dumb it down a bit). Thanks
Answer: If it's an ellipse the area is pi*r1*r2, r1 and r2 being the semimajor and semiminor axes. This is 3.14*25*9 ~= 705 sq. ft. You'll have to estimate the average depth. If it's 4 feet you have 4*705 ~= 2820 cu ft. There are ~7.5 gallons in a cu ft, so that's 7.5*2820 ~= 21200 gallons.

label: Science & Mathematics
sentence:
Question: how friction is responsible for reducing the effort required in lifting weights in pulleys?
Answer: My answer is somewhat silly.

I think that is friction between the rope and your hands. If there was low friction, the rope would slide out, or you would have to hold it very very tightly, and this would increase the effort.

As between the pulley and the rope, there is very little friction and exactly this reduces the effort. If the friction was high (e.g. if the pulley was stuck), the required effort would have been higher.

If you're interested in how the wheel reduces friction, it is simple. Say you need to pull something by many meters. If there was no wheel, you would have many meters of high friction movement. If you have a wheel with a circumference of 1m, and its axis has a circumference of 1cm, then for each rotation of the wheel (1m) only the axis slides against the wheel by 1cm. The slide distance is 100 times lower. That's even not accounting for sleeve bearings (reducing friction of the axis). Or, even better, ball bearings.

Title: Why does the Moon orbit the Earth?
Question: Challenge:

If it's because of gravity, then why doesn't the moon just crash into Earth?
Answer: Objects orbit one another because they have a curved trajectory that results from the vector addition of their momentum (in the direction of travel, tangential to the orbit) and the gravitational attraction to the other object (normal to the orbit).

This vector is constantly changing in direction (but not to any significant degree in magnitude) because of the object's motion, but it always keeps the satellite's acceleration pointed towards the object is it orbiting, resulting in smooth, roughly circular motion.

clear tape is ok.  It will work if you have no other options.

Answer: Insulin promotes the expression of glucose receptors at the cell surface.  This mechanism is indirect; insulin binds to its receptor and promotes glucose transporter expression on the cell surface.  No glucose transporter - glucose can't get into the cell (the cell membrane is essentially impermiable to glucose).  Note that brain and liver are insensitive to insulin.

Question: How would I find the vector potential, A, of a uniform magnetic field?
Answer: The vector potential is defined only to within the gradient of a scalar. That is, you can add the gradient of any scalar field to the answer below and get an equally valid expression for the vector potential.

If B is the constant (vector) value of the magnetic field then the vector potential is:

A(r) = -r x (B/2)

where r is the the position vector and x means cross product. In Cartesian coordinates in which the magnetic field is pointing in the direction of the z axis, the three components of A are:

A_x = -(B/2)y
A_y = (B/2)x
A_z = 0

where B here is a constant number.

Question: give me details in starting a new export business and the requirements to start it?
Answer: You should first find a competitive productive activity (manufacturing or natural resources) in your location and then try to establish a relationship with the providers, this activity may be, for example, artcrafts.  then you have to visit craftman in your location and show interest in buying their products.

International clients are highly demanding, so you must carefully consider build a poll of providers that guarrantee you: quality, quantities and reliability.

Once you have selected the provider then you have the first half (but the most difficult is to come)  now you have to build trust in potential buyers abroad of the product you selected to export.

In my experience I founded very useful the help of my country embassy in other countries, as well as this I highly recommend you to build an online (and printed) catalog. You should be extra careful with details in those marketing materials, NO typos, no false statements, try to be as accurate as possible and, of course, try to have those materials in at least two languages. Also be ready with quotation templates and check the payment method best suits you. again trust is important in this regard.

In this stage you may find in statistics about export of your country (given in any Economy Ministery website) about top foreign countries that most likely buy the kind of products you choose to sell from your location, keep it simple but be persistent as it takes a lot of work to get the first order, however, once you start, yopu will be in one of the most lucratives activities of the world and prosper you, as well as your family.

As you don´t give further details in your question I assume that you are starting from scratch, so, don´t worry, try to strenght relations with your friends and family, and the friends of your friends and the family of your family, try to find in your personal network those fellows that may help you connect the chain (find the best provider or find the first client) in any case prepare your selling speech for each case and be ready to show leadership and motivation, remember that doing business is a human activity and in involves inter-personal relationship skills.

Also, remember to keep it simple, export follows the same principle of local selling, you buy as cheap as possible and sell as expensive as possible (your profit will be the difference)

buy cheap and sell expensive (but be fair in both sides)

Don´t kill the gold eggs chicken by trying to get all the eggs at once, keep you baance and try to not be so greedy.

Title: Can u send a fax from your computer if u have Cable?
Question: I don't have a fax machine, i am using the built in Microsoft Fax console, but can never send a fax. My comuter has a built in fax modem. My computer makes a tone, but of course I don't have a phone line hooked up because I am using cable to access internet. So, Do I also need to pug in a phone line then? If so can I just hook line straight from wall jack to computer? Also, when I type in the number to be dialed do I put in dashes or spaces?
Answer: For starters, make sure you're plugging your cable from your wall to the correct jack in your modem.  One usually has a phone icon - don't use that one for the wall connection.  Use that for an actual phone.

If your hear a dial tone from your speakers when you try to fax someone, then that's a good thing - your fax is trying to start up and dial.  If you don't hear a dial tone, again check your plugs.  It may even help to check the wall outlet as well, since that may be part of the problem.

As for dialing, you can usually go either way with dashes or no dashes.  Just be sure to use area codes where necessary.

Now be warned - sometimes sending a fax over a cable modem won't work out.  I've had that told to me once, and it turned out that it did work in my case.  But then recently, I tried to fax and they didn't go through all the way.  I had to do some fancy trickery to get things right again, but it worked out in the end.

BTW, the link below is from Microsoft's website.  It may help with some minor usage and troubleshooting.

label: Science & Mathematics
sentence:
Question: Can diffusion take place in solids?
Answer: Yes.

Orthoclase feldspar is an example.  At high temperatures, Fe will fit into the orthoclase lattice.  As temperature drops, the lattice shrinks so that Fe no longer fits.  Fe diffuses out of the latice and accumulates along the planes between orthoclase crystal twins.  Along the way, it grabs O to produce Fe2O3.  If you look closely at pink granite, usually you will see that the pink grains are actually white and red striped.  Those grains are orthoclase crystals with exsolved hematite along twin planes.

Exsolution and diffusion of Fe from orthoclase can only occur at high temperature.  If the orthoclase cools too quickly for the Fe to diffuse out, it will remain in the orthoclase lattice, which will be distorted to accomodate the larger (larger than K) Fe ion.

Material science is not boring.

sentence:
Title: I have to do a report on animal rights and animal cruelty. Any opinions?
Question: I need to right about what myself and others think about animal rights and cruelty, and if it's right or wrong.
Answer: With animal rights and animal cruelty, it's often not a simple 'yes' or 'no' question, not a simple matter of 'right' or 'wrong'.  There are many degrees.

If you are talking about animal rights, what rights should an animal be afforded?  Does an animal have the same rights as a human?  Do all animals get the same levels of rights?  Does a single ant have the same right to life and liberty that a human, or even a dog does?  How about a starfish?  A sponge?  An amoeba?

At what level do you make the arbitrary decision that 'this organism has a right to exist, but this one doesn't?'

Does the Ebola virus have a right to exist and propagate itself?  If you don't agree a virus has the right to live, how about Cochliomyia hominivorax, the human screwworm?  Should you allow treatment of humans infested with intestinal parasites?

Where do you draw the line?

The same can be said for animal cruelty.  Who gets to decide what's cruel?  How exactly do you define cruelty?  Is dropping a kitten in boiling water cruel?  Most people would say yes.  How about dropping a mosquito larva in boiling water?  Or a lobster?  It's cruel to keep a kitten in a jar on your desk, but how about a goldfish?

As with most things in life, there is no easy answer.  Certainly, there should be some benefit, some gain to humanity that must be demonstrated in order to justify killing another organism, but what level of justification is required?  

Is squirting caustic substances in a bunny's eyes justified if it means we can develop a substance that won't burn a child's eyes?  

Is killing hundreds of thousands, even millions of mosquitoes justified if it keeps one person from dying from West Nile virus?  How about if it means you can have a backyard BBQ without being driven inside by biting flies?

Is shooting a deer justified if it means that a family can eat for a month off the meat?  How about if some guy just really wants to kill something and put its head on his rec room wall?  How about if the deer are so overpopulated that they are becoming diseased and the overall health of the whole population is declining because they have eaten all the available forage?

There are no easy answers.

Question: What continent was the doodo bird native to?
Answer: The dodo or dronte (scientific name Raphus cucullatus) was a flightless bird native only to the island of Mauritius in the Indian Ocean. The dodo was a flightless member of the pigeon family. Fully grown dodos weighted about 23 kg (50 pounds). Around 1505 the Portuguese became the first Europeans to discover the dodo. By 1681 it had been driven to extinction by humans and the feral dogs, pigs, rats, and monkeys introduced by Europeans to Mauritius. The dodo was not the only Mauritian bird driven to extinction in recent centuries. Of the 45 bird species originally found, only 21 still survive. Two bird species closely related to the dodo also became extinct: the Reunion solitaire by 1746, and the Rodrigues solitaire by 1790. sentence:
Title: What type of growth or decay function does one encounter in work or in personal life?
Question: This is in regards to exponential and logarithmic applications in mathematics.  I need some examples of either so I can better understand the concepts in real-life or real-world scenarios.
Answer: 1.  The von Bertalanffy growth function (VBGF) introduced by von Bertalanffy in 1938 predicts the length of a shark as a function of its age, L = L(t): L(t) = Loo - (Loo - Lo) exp(-kt) 
2.  Examples of exponential growth
Biology. 
Microorganisms in a culture dish will grow exponentially, at first, after the first microorganism appears (but then logistically until the available food is exhausted, when growth stops). 
A virus (SARS, West Nile, smallpox) of sufficient infectivity (k > 0) will spread exponentially at first, if no artificial immunization is available. Each infected person can infect multiple new people. 
Human population, if the number of births and deaths per person per year were to remain constant (but also see logistic growth). 
Many responses of living beings to stimuli, including human perception, are logarithmic responses, which are the inverse of exponential responses; the loudness and frequency of sound are perceived logarithmically, even with very faint stimulus, within the limits of perception. This is the reason that exponentially increasing the brightness of visual stimuli is perceived by humans as a smooth (linear) increase, rather than an exponential increase. This has survival value. Generally it is important for the organisms to respond to stimuli in a wide range of levels, from very low levels, to very high levels, while the accuracy of the estimation of differences at high levels of stimulus is much less important for survival. 
Electroengineering 
Charging and discharging of capacitors and changes in current in inductors are also exponential growth and decay phenomena. Engineers use a rule of five time constants to estimate when a steady state has been reached. 
Computer technology 
Processing power of computers. See also Moore's law and technological singularity (under exponential growth, there are no such singularities). 
Internet traffic growth. 
Wikipedia:Modelling Wikipedia's growth - an analysis of Wikipedia's growth rates based on article growth rates and other statistics 
Investment. The effect of compound interest over many years has a substantial effect on savings and a person's ability to retire. See also rule of 72 
Physics 
Atmospheric pressure decreases exponentially with increasing height above sea level, at a rate of about 12% per 1000m. 
Nuclear chain reaction (the concept behind nuclear weapons). Each uranium nucleus that undergoes fission produces multiple neutrons, each of which can be absorbed by adjacent uranium atoms, causing them to fission in turn. If the probability of neutron absorption exceeds the probability of neutron escape (a function of the shape and mass of the uranium), k > 0 and so the production rate of neutrons and induced uranium fissions increases exponentially, in an uncontrolled reaction. 
Newton's law of cooling  where T is temperature, t is time, and, A, D, and k > 0 are constants, is an example of exponential decay. 
Multi-level marketing 
Exponential increases appear in each level of a starting member's downline as each subsequent member recruits more people.

Question: What happened in Munich,Germany in 1972?
Answer: The summer Olympic games, during which Arab terrorists belonging to the PLO faction called Black September snuck into the athletes village, captured nine Israeli hostages and after their demands for the freedom of 200 Arab prisoners and safe passage out of Germany were not met, they accepted a deal to take helicopters to the airport at a NATO airbase, where they and the hostages would be flown to Cairo.

After the helicopters landed at the air base around 10:30 p.m., German sharpshooters attempted to kill the terrorists and a bloody firefight ensued. At 11, the media was mistakenly informed that the hostages had been saved and the news was announced to a relieved Israeli public. Almost an hour later, however, new fighting broke out and one of the helicopters holding the Israelis was blown up by a terrorist grenade. The remaining hostages in the second helicopter were shot to death by one of the surviving terrorists.

At 3 a.m., a drawn and teary-eyed Jim McKay, who had been reporting the drama throughout the day as part of ABC's Olympic coverage, announced: "They're all gone."

Five of the terrorists were killed along with one policeman, and three were captured. A little over a month later, on Oct. 29, a Lufthansa jet was hijacked by terrorists demanding that the Munich killers be released.

The Germans capitulated and the terrorists were let go, but an Israeli assassination squad was assigned to track them down along with those responsible for planning the massacre. According to George Jonas in Vengeance: The True Story of an Israeli Counter-Terrorist Team, eight of the 11 men targeted for death were killed. Of the remaining three, one died of natural causes and the other two were assassinated, but it is not known for sure if they were killed by Israeli agents.

label: Health
sentence:
Question: Do these "diets" really work? Like Slimquick and any others you can think of.?
Answer: Any diet will work, keep in mind the following before choosing your next diet:

Diets and changing your eating to healthy food choices can work but because we know so little about ourselves and our relationship with food, it makes it difficult to win the battle. A lot of us have problems with dieting because we have a problem called "emotional eating" we eat to comfort ourselves during difficult, stressful, sad, etc times in our lives.

You may experience all those emotions during dieting as we continuously get on the scale hoping to see a big difference in numbers after dieting only for a day or two. Also what is stressful when dieting is that we try to lose a large number of weight in such a short period of time which in most cases is unreasonable. 

This all brings about stress, discomfort and sadness. When we feel this way, we turn to our best friend for help and support which for many of us is food. The diet is now broken and we feel that we can't stick to diets. We then try fad diet after fad diet hoping to lose the original 20 pounds and now we may have as much as 30 pounds to lose because we continue to put on weight as we continue to break these fad diets by binging before starting our next diet. 

Please learn about your relationship with food before your next diet so that you may achieve your goals. To help a little, keep in mind the following:

You already know how to lose weight. You know that if you eat less and exercise more eventually you’ll see the pounds come off. What’s getting in your way? Why do you usually regain the weight you lost? The answer to all these questions is the same “Emotional Eating.” Simply defined, emotional eating means you eat to satisfy emotional hunger; it means you use food for comfort or as a way to cope with life; and it means you eat for reasons other than what your body needs. Whenever you reach for a boredom-breaking snack despite your commitment, or whenever you eat to quell anxiety, that’s emotional eating. Whenever you binge after a fight, or double up on portions because your day turned sour, that’s emotional eating. Whenever you feel that sharp craving for your favorite food, that’s emotional eating. When we eat during these times while on a diet, we believe the diet doesn’t work or that we lack self control and then look for the quickest way to lose weight (fasting/diet pills, ect) after eating all we can since we already messed the diet day up. Read the information below but remember that emotional eating plays a big part in why we don’t continue dieting and why we regain lost weight and why we binge today and start a new diet tomorrow. Best of Luck.

P.S. After learning about my relationship with food, I was able to drop my weight from 263 pounds down to 151 pounds which is a 112 pound weight lost.

label: Science & Mathematics
sentence:
Question: how does A. Einstien come up with the equation E=mc2? how will it be ralative in dev. of a-bomb/fusion?
Answer: The E=mc^2 equations come from Einstein's theory of Special Relativity. Special Relativity concerns the laws of motion and observed properties when objects are travelling very close to the speed of light.

Special relativity starts with two premises: the speed of light is constant for all observers, and the laws of physics are the same for all observers. However, observed properties are not necessarily the same.

Say I flew past the Earth in a space ship travelling 99% the speed of light. To me, the space ship is normal, but the Earth would look squished, rotated, and blue with everyone moving slowly. To you, however, Earth would look normal, but the space ship would be squished, rotated, blue and with everyone moving very slowly. (This gets resolved if the space ship turns around - breaking the symmetry - to come home, and results in the famous Twins "Paradox.")

In describing the laws of motion in the context of special relativity Einstein derived that E = mc^2 -- in other words that mass has a "rest energy."

If an electron and an anti-matter electron (known as the positron) bump into each other then their is total energy conversion. The mass of two electrons is converted into energy.

In a fission or fusion bomb the the atomic process (breaking apart a heavy atom, or fusing some light atoms) results in a  much smaller conversion of mass to energy. But still a lot compared with normal explosives.

Title: who is more inteligent to answer this question ?(I have answer I need the way of solution.?
Question: a little object from heigh h release freely and at the last moment of falling, came down 44/1 m.indicate the heigh h (g:9/8 m/s2 )   (the answer:  122/5)
Answer: Given v_i = initial velocity = 0; v_f = final velocity = 44 m/s; a = 9.8 m/s^2:

dv/dt = a = 9.8 m/s^2
dv = 9.8 dt
int(dv, v_0, v_f) = int(9.8 dt, 0, t)
v_f - v_0 = 9.8t
44 - 0 = 9.8t
t = 44/9.8 = 440/98 = 220/49

int(dv, v_0, v) = int(9.8dt, 0, t)
ds/dt = v = 9.8t
ds = 9.8tdt
int(ds, 0, h) = int(9.8tdt, 0, 220/49)
h = 4.9(220/49)^2/2 = (49*22*220)/(49*49*2) = (11*220)/49 = (2200 + 220)/49 = 2420/49 ~ 49.3878

Alternatively, since accelration was constant, you could always get it more quickly with the formulas that were derived with integrals as above:

v_f = v_0 + at
s = v_0t + 1/2at^2

Either way you should get 2420/49 m if the initial conditions are correct.  I don't know where 122/5 comes from although it seems to be approximately a half of this answer.

label: Health
sentence:
Question: If my mom has diabetes 2 am i at risk to?
Answer: Whoa... I can see there is a lot of misunderstanding about diabetes.  The thing you need to know is that there are two types of diabetes.

Type 1 Diabetes presents more commonly during early childhood or early puberty but can occur at any age.  Type 1 specifically refers to diabetes resulting from the destruction of insulin-secreting cells in your pancreas.  All Type 1 diabetics require insulin because their body no longer makes it.

Type 2 Diabetes presents more commonly in adulthood but can occur at any age and is being seen in younger and younger patients.  Type 2 specifically refers to diabetes resulting from your body's becoming more resistant (or less sensitive) to the insulin that your pancreas produces.  Most patients can be treated with oral medications that improve your body's sensitivity to your endogenous insulin or stimulate more insulin release from your pancreas.  Type 2 diabetics have high levels of insulin circulating unlike Type 1 diabetics.  Some Type 2 diabetics may go on to need insulin if their oral medications are not adequately controlling their sugars; most will be on a combination of insulin and oral meds.

Both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes are multifactorial.  There are both genetic and environmental factors that lead to the disease.  Therefore, just because one identical twin has diabetes (either kind) does not necessarily mean that the other will get it as well!

Population studies have shown that for Type 1 diabetes...
If your mom has Type 1 DM - your risk is 1 in 17
If your mom has Type 1 DM and had you before age 25 - your risk 1 in 25
If your mom has Type 1 DM and had you after age 25 - your risk 1 in 100
If your mom got Type 1 DM before she was 11 - the above risk doubles
If both your parents have Type 1 DM - your risk is 1 in 5

For Type 2 diabetes...
If you have one parent who had Type 2 DM before 50 - your risk is 1 in 7
If you have one parent who had Type 2 DM after 50 - your risk is 1 in 13
If you have two parents with Type 2 DM - your risk is 1 in 2
If you have an identical twin with Type 2 DM - your risk is 3 in 4

This information is all available from the American Diabetes Association.  As you can see, Type 2 diabetes actually has a higher inherited risk than Type 1!  There are things that you can do to minimize your chances of developing Type 2 DM, though, even though you are at risk.  That includes regular exercise, maintenance of a healthy weight, and reducing fat and calorie intake.  There are also some medications that can reduce your risk of developing Type 2 DM; you should talk to your doctor about whether these would be appropriate for you.  Above all, don't worry!  You are expressing concern about your health which is the FIRST STEP!  If you are motivated to take the appropriate steps towards maintaining your health, the odds of preventing diabetes are in your favor!!  Good luck!

EDIT:
To justwannaknow - I think what you say is misleading.  The AMA's recommendation in 2002 was for people to take a daily multivitamin.  There is still no recommendation for physicians to advise patients to take herbal supplements and other nutritional supplements like "Glycoscience".

To hmt42play - Islet cell transplants are not being recommended for patients with Type 2 diabetes!!!  As you diabetes educator, you should be aware of this!  Type 2 diabetics generally have functioning islet cells and DO produce insulin.  The problem is with insulin resistance so giving them more islet cells would not resolve the underlying problem.  Islet cell transplants are currently only being used in unstable Type 1 diabetics.  Please do not give this poor woman the idea that islet cell transplantation is a cure for Type 2 diabetes!

label: Science & Mathematics
sentence:
Title: What are the dimensions (length, width, and height or thickness) of the physical universe (in light years)?
Question: Basically, how big is the universe?  If not actually known at this time, is the actual size of the entire universe considered to be knowable (i.e. that there is some possibility of measuring or estimating its size but the techniques are not currently available).

I've read that the universe is thought to be "saddle shaped"
and expanding at an accelerating rate.  If I correctly understand some research that I've done in Wickipedia, the rate of expansion of the universe is 70 (km/s)/Mps or 70 kilometers per second per megaparsec [i.e. million parsecs].

I don't understand parsecs, except that they are a measurement of distance similar to light years.  Also, I don't understand the megaparsec part of the expansion rate. What does it mean for example, to say that the universe is expanding at a rate of 70 kilometers per second per (x number of light years)?

One more thing, I was not able to find a rate of acceleration of expansion. Would the form be increase of distance of expansion/s/s?
Answer: "...What are the dimensions (length, width, and height or thickness) of the physical universe (in light years)?..."
The universe can't be measured in terms of length, width, and height. Such parameters require some reference point from which measurements can be made, along with some distant boundary where the measurement would end. You simply can't do that with the universe because the universe is isotropic, meaning it's the same in all directions from any observing point. From Earth we can look outward in any direction and 'see' about 13.7-billion light years. From Earth that represents a boundary. Here comes the tricky part: if some alien in a galaxy 13.7-billion light years away from Earth looked outward in all directions (including back towards Earth) they'd 'see' a universe that appeared to be 13.7-billion light years in scope. In other words, the universe has no boundary. To have one it would have to be inside some "thing" else, and there's absolutely no evidence that such is the case.

To confuse the issue even more, if we had the ultimate telescope with limitless viewing power we still will never be able to see into the universe beyond a certain range. That's because at almost the same instant of the Big Bang the universe briefly expanded faster than light (this doesn't violate relativity because it was the space of the universe that did the expanding). In our 'normal' universe the speed of light is the speed limit which prevents us from ever seeing any of that inflation because it's moving away faster than the speed of light.
-----------------------------------------------------------
"...I've read that the universe is thought to be "saddle shaped..."
More recent observations point more towards the universe being geometrically "flat." This simply means that the universe appears to be infinite, that its space will expand forever while cooling more and more over the eons.
------------------------------------------------------------
"...What does it mean for example, to say that the universe is expanding at a rate of 70 kilometers per second per (x number of light years)?..."
You've described the so-called Hubble Constant. (70 km/sec/Mpc) It means if galaxy 'A' is 1 Mpc (1-million ly) away from us it's recessional velocity will be 70 km/sec. If galaxy 'B' is 2 Mpc away then it's velocity will be 140 km/sec It's important to keep in mind though that it's space that's expanding like that, not the galaxies moving THROUGH space; they just get carried along.
------------------------------------------------------------
"...I was not able to find a rate of acceleration of expansion..."
I've been looking for a figure too. So far the only thing I've come up with is -3.15^36 /sec/sec  Darned if I know what the units of measurement are though. Maybe someone else on Yahoo can help us out with that.

Answer: look at the noted citation

    What Is Atrial Septal Defect? 
An atrial septal defect (ASD) is a hole in the wall (septum) that separates the two upper chambers (atria) of the heart. The defect allows blood to flow from one atrium to the other, usually from the left side to the right side. This causes extra blood flow:

In the right atrium 
In the right ventricle 
To the lungs 


Figure A shows the normal anatomy and blood flow of the interior of the heart. Figure B shows a heart with an atrial septal defect, which allows oxygen-rich blood from the left atrium to mix with oxygen-poor blood from the right atrium. 

In a normal heart, oxygen-poor (blue) blood returns from the body to the right atrium. From the right atrium, the blue blood flows to the right ventricle—one of the two lower chambers of the heart—and is pumped to the lungs to pick up oxygen. After traveling through the lungs, the blood is now oxygen-rich and red. The red blood returns from the lungs to the left atrium and goes to the left ventricle, where it is pumped to the body. The right and left sides of the heart are normally completely separated by the septum. The septum keeps the blue blood from mixing with the red blood. The later section "How the Heart Works" explains the process in greater detail.

ASD is the second most common congenital heart defect.

More than 3,000 babies are born with ASD each year in the United States. 
ASD occurs twice as often in girls as in boys. 
Effects of Atrial Septal Defect
Over time, the extra blood flow to the right side of the heart and the lungs can cause:

Enlargement of the right atrium and the right ventricle. 
Right heart overload. The right side of the heart has to work harder to pump extra blood to the lungs, especially as resistance in the pulmonary (PULL-mun-ary) artery increases. Over time, the heart may become overworked, and function may become impaired. This is exceedingly rare with modern methods of diagnosis and treatment. 
Irregular heartbeats or rhythms (arrhythmias). Extra blood flowing into the right atrium through the ASD can cause the atrium to stretch and enlarge. When this occurs, a fast heartbeat can develop with symptoms such as dizziness, fainting, or chest discomfort. 
Stroke. Occasionally a blood clot in a vein or in the right side of the heart can pass through the ASD and enter the blood stream, where it can block an artery supplying the brain and cause a stroke. 
Pulmonary artery hypertension. This is when high blood pressure exists in the arteries that carry blood to the lungs. The extra blood being pumped to the lungs can increase the pressure in the pulmonary arteries. Over time, high pressure can damage the arteries and the small blood vessels in the lungs. They thicken and become stiff, making it harder for blood to flow through them (pulmonary vascular disease). 
Usually, most of these effects don’t show up until adulthood, often around age 30 or later. They are rare in infants and children.

Characteristics
An ASD is classified by its size and location.

Size
The size of an ASD can range from small to large.

Most small defects close on their own as the heart grows during childhood. They usually allow only a small amount of blood to flow between the atria. 
Moderate to large defects are much less likely to close on their own. They allow two or more times the normal amount of blood to flow through the right side of the heart. Large holes sometimes cause symptoms during infancy or childhood. 
Location
Three major types of ASD exist, based on the location of the defect on the septum:

Secundum. This defect is in the middle of the septum. It is the most common form of ASD. About 7 out of every 10 babies born with ASD have this type. This type often closes on its own, unless it is large.

Title: SQL GROUP BY clause giving me grief AGAIN!?
Question: I don't know why I can never get a GROUP BY to work properly. I'm sure it's something really simple. Please help! Here is the query.

SELECT t4_key FROM rw_top40 GROUP BY t4_key WHERE year=97 AND season='2 - Summer' ORDER BY t4_key, year, season, month, day

Error is the normal, you have an error in you syntax blah blah blah. The t4_key column is a variable length string. If that's the problem, how do I duplicate the effects of group by on a text field?
Answer: From what it looks like you want to do, I don't think you even need the GROUP BY clause. You probably want something like:

SELECT t4_key, year, season, month, day
FROM rw_top40
WHERE year = 97 AND season = '2 - summer'
ORDER BY t4_key, year, season, month, day;

Anyway, the GROUP BY clause has to come AFTER the WHERE clause, like this:

SELECT t4_key, count(*)
FROM rw_top40
WHERE year = 97
GROUP BY t4_key

Question: osteoporosis what is a chroinc and acute example for osteoporosis?
Answer: Osteoporosis is a disease of bone in which the bone mineral density (BMD) is reduced, bone microarchitecture is disrupted, and the amount and variety of non-collagenous proteins in bone is altered. Osteoporotic bones are more susceptible to fracture. Osteoporosis is defined by the World Health Organization (WHO) as either a bone mineral density 2.5 standard deviations below peak bone mass (20-year-old sex-matched healthy person average) as measured by DXA, or any fragility fracture. While treatment modalities are becoming available (such as the bisphosphonates), prevention is still considered the most important way to reduce fracture. Due to its hormonal component, more women, particularly after menopause, suffer from osteoporosis than men. In addition it may be caused by various hormonal conditions, smoking and medications (specifically glucocorticoids).\n\nclick here:http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteoporosis#Signs_and_symptoms

Question: why is salt use to melt the snow?
Answer: Couple good answers there. The ones about lowering the freezing point are good, but not quite there. If it just lowered the freezing point (which is true) it would never melt the ice/snow, since it nothing has affected the temperature yet. What happens is that the first interaction of salt and ice/snow (water) causes heat to be released, it is an exothermic reaction. That little bit of heat allows more ice to melt, reacting with more salt, creating more heat, melting more ice, etc. So it is the exothermic reaction that causes the melting, the lower freezing point keeps it from refreezing.

sentence:
Question: Which direction does a twister twist in, clockwise or counter-clockwise? does hemisphere change that?
Answer: In the Northern Hemisphere, a tornado or twister twists counter-clockwise. In the Southern Hemisphere is clockwise. This is due to the Coriolis effect, caused when objects (in this case air) moves over the rotating earth. The air flows towards the twister, but curves to right (relative to the direction it is flowing). It is easier to visualize if you think about some air flowing straight north to a twister. Since the earth's surface is moving faster towards the east where it started, it carry on some of the momentum and curve to the east (right of the northerly direction it was flowing). This will tend to cause the air to miss the twister, but he extreme low pressure will allow the higher pressure around it to bend the flow towards the funnel, but the air will have the angular momentum of moving the right as it moves in, thus creating the counter-clockwise twist. In the Southern Hemisphere, a flow from the south towards a twister will be coming from a place closer to the earth's axis, and thus will be moving East more slowly than the land under the twister, so it fall behind (to the West) as it approaches, resulting, through the similar process as described above, in a clockwise twist.

Title: Should i trade Eli Manning for Micheal vick?
Question: i think i should.  Vick is a solid QB
Answer: Not a good week for either of them. That makes for a tough trade. I say trade for Vick though. He's a multidimensional player. If your league gives you points for rushing yards, scoop him up. 

Michael Vick has struggled in his last two games, and that should continue here. The Ravens have the kind of defense that makes things tough on quarterbacks; they have an aggressive secondary, and they bring a lot of pressure. For the season, they're allowing opponents to complete only 53 percent of their passes (3rd-lowest in the league), with twice as many interceptions (18) as touchdowns (9). They also rank among the leaders with 25 sacks. And with a lot of speed at linebacker, they're one of the few defenses that Vick might not run very successfully against. When Atlanta played Baltimore four years ago, Vick completed only 12 of 24 passes and finished with minus-5 rushing yards on his seven rushing attempts. In his three preseason appearances against them since that time, Vick has completed only 2 of 7 passes and run for only 8 yards on 2 carries, with 1 interception, 1 lost fumble and one broken leg. So this definitely looks like a game where he might put up some of his worst numbers of the season.

Manning is struggling. He's thrown only 2 TDs and completed just 52 percent of his passes in his last three games, and all of those were in the friendly confines of Giants Stadium. He hasn't thrown for even 180 yards in any of those games. Tough to see him rebounding on the road against one of the league's better defenses. The Jaguars have been especially tough at home, allowing only 4 TDs -- and a total of 37 points -- in five games. They also shut down a good Eagles offense in Philadelphia back in week 8. Manning is also dealing with the loss of Amani Toomer, out for the season with a knee injury, and will now be without left tackle Luke Petitgout, who broke his fibula last week and should miss the remainder of the season. One thing that can be said for Manning is that being on the road might help his game somewhat. The winds at the Meadowlands can wreak havoc with passing games; poor weather has been a factor in Manning's lesser numbers of late. Manning has posted far better numbers on the road thus far: 5 TDs and 4 interceptions in five home games, versus 10 TDs and 7 interceptions in four road games. With that said, though, only one of those four opponents, Dallas in week 7, had a defense the caliber of Jacksonville's. Don't expect big numbers from Manning in this one.

Title: two disks that can rotate about their centres like a merry-go-?
Question: two disks that can rotate about their centres like a merry-go-round. At time t = 0, the reference lines of the two disks have the same orientation. Disk A is already rotating, with a constant angular velocity of 9.5 rad/s. Disk B has been stationary but now begins to rotate at a constant angular acceleration of 2.2 rad/s2. (a) At what time t will the reference lines of the two disks momentarily have the same angular displacement θ ? (b) Will that time t be the first time since t = 0 that the reference lines are momentarily aligned?
Answer: The equations of motion for the angular displacement of each disk are given by:

Disk A: R1(t) = (1/2)*alpha1*t² + w1*t +Ri1
Disk B: R2(t) = (1/2)*alpha2*t² + w2*t +Ri2

For part (a), we're looking for the time, T, for which R1(T) = R2(T)

(1/2)*alpha1*T² + w1*T +Ri1 = (1/2)*alpha2*T² + w2*T +Ri2

From the problem statement, we obtain the following information:

Ri1 = Ri2
alpha1 = 0
w1 = 9.5 rad/s
alpha2 = 2.2 rad/s²
w2 = 0

Substituting these values and simplifying, we obtain:

w1*T= (1/2)*alpha2*T²

w1= (1/2)*alpha2*T

T = 2*w1 / (alpha2)

T = 2(9.5 rad/s) / (2.2 rad/s²)

T = 8.64 s

Technically, part (b) is impossible to say without knowing how the reference line is defined, but I'll give it a whirl. If the reference line is measured from the center of each disk to its outer edge, then yes.

However, if the reference line is placed across the diameter of the disk, then no. In this case, the reference lines will be aligned when the angular displacement of Disk A is 180° or pi radians ahead of Disk B. To solve for this time, simply add pi to Disk B's equation of motion:

(1/2)*alpha1*T² + w1*T +Ri1 = (1/2)*alpha2*T² + w2*T +Ri2 + pi

Substituting out known values again leads us to:

w1*T= (1/2)*alpha2*T² + pi

or:

(1/2)*alpha2*T² - w1*T + pi = 0

1.1*T² - 9.5*T + pi = 0

Using the quadratic formula, we find that 

T = .344 seconds or 8.292 seconds

Thus, if the reference line is directed across the entire disk, then they are momentarily aligned twice before having the same angular displacement.

(This added after a while)
{BTW, monohan47130 - no I didn't. Please read what I wrote. If the reference lines are defined along the radius only, then you are correct - there is only one point at which the disks have the same angular displacement. But, reference lines are typically made along the entire circle (diameter). This means that they will be aligned 3 times total in 8.64 seconds :) }

Question: What role do enzymes play in medical diagnosis?
Answer: Enzyme levels are frequently measured in blood samples to determine if a person has had a heart attack.  Normally these enzymes are not present in the blood, but they are released into the blood stream as cardiac (heart) cells die as a result of the heart attack.  The cell bursts when it dies and spills the enzymes into the blood stream.  So when these enzymes are present, it means there has been cardiac cell death, and therefore a heart attack.

Question: what does place only betting mean in horse racing?
Answer: Place only betting means that there is no show betting in the race.
Just win and place because there are not enough horses in the race to allow for show betting.

This is because the track feels it would lose money if they allowed show betting.

99.9% of all races have win ,place and show betting.

If you bet a horse to win he has to win in order for you to win money.

If you bet a horse to place you will get money if he wins or places(comes in 2nd)

If you bet a horse to show(comes in 3rd) you will get money if he wins,places or shows.

In most cases but not always a horse will pay more to win and less for 2nd and even less for 3rd becuase of the pool money bet in the race.

To put it simply when you bet on a horse he has to finsih as well or better than you bet him for in order for you to cash your ticket.

Title: a planetary nebula exists before what?
Question: before the red giant phases.
before the main sequence.
for a long duration compared to the time the star spent on the main sequence.
or all the above.
Answer: A Planetary Nebula is a misleading name.  At the end of a lower mass star's life (for stars up to about 8 times the mass of the sun), the star puffs up, and loses the outer layers of gas surrounding it.  All this gas goes out into space where it can be seen as what we call a planetary nebula.

Originally the word "nebula" was applied to any astronomical object that was not a star or a memeber of our solar system (planets, asteroids etc), the word essentially means "cloud."

As telescopes got better people started to find many different types of nebulae. A Spiral Nebula looks like, well a spiral, today we know that these are spiral galaxies.  Planetary Nebula were named because the looked round, and a number of them had the same greenish color that Uranus had been seen to have by Hershel.

Question: A Man carries some dollars in his pocket and goes to the church and prays, Oh Jesus, Please double my dollars and I shall donate eight of those to the church. Title: Why would a defendant use a Brady motion?

Answer: Dear Friend,

A Brady motion generally means that the defendant believes the police or prosecutor has withheld evidence which would tend to show his innocence.  Often, this is in the context of asking for a mistrial or appealing a conviction.  On the basis of what you've told us in this case, I could see a defense lawyer saying that "I wasn't able to give my client his fair day in court because the other side hid this evidence which would make any fair jury doubt the motives of this officer -- so let's start again from square one."  If successful, a Brady motion could result in a new trial, or at least another chance to present defense evidence.

Yours in Him,
Francesois

Question: What was your biggest Thanksgiving disaster - and how could you have prevented it?
Answer: It was the first Thanksgiving after my husband and I started dating.  He drove three hours to spend the holiday weekend with me so I wanted to impress him with a home cooked meal.  I waited until leaving work Wednesday night to go the the grocery store and in the mad push of people, I reached in the bin and grabbed a turkey.  The next afternoon, I placed my turkey in a sink full of water to thaw and began on my side dishes.  After he arrived and we had a drink, he ventured into the kitchen at which point I noticed he was peering down into the sink and frowning.  I asked if something was wrong with the turkey and he said "Yeah . . . it's a duck."  

To my horror, I had picked up a duck and never noticed that this long narrow bird was not a fat round turkey.  I attempted to roast it and while it had a nice flavor, we quickly realized there isn't much meat on a duck.  In addition, my gravy was burnt, my potatoes were salty and the macaroni and cheese was a solid block.  I finally accepted defeat and we ventured out to the local 7-Eleven and had a Thanksgiving hot dog!   

I wouldn't have done a thing to prevent it!!  That night my husband told me he loved me for the first time and we have been together for over twelve years.  He turned out to be an incredible cook and  I have never cooked another Thanksgiving dinner!  And every year we toast our famous Thanksgiving duck!

Question: What is a kundalini or sokrlung experience. I meditated for two months and felt warm now i have mental illness
Answer: Asian traditions recognize a number of pitfalls associated with intensive meditation practice, such as altered perceptions that can be frightening, and "false enlightenment," associated with delightful or terrifying visions (Epstein, 1990). Epstein (1990) describes a "specific mental disorder that the Tibetans call 'sokrlung' (a disorder of the 'life-bearing wind that supports the mind' that can arise as a consequence...of strain[ing] too tightly in an obsessive way to achieve moment-to-moment awareness" (p. 27). When meditative practices are transplanted into Western contexts, the same problems can occur. Anxiety, dissociation, depersonalization, altered perceptions, agitation, and muscular tension have been observed in western meditation practitioners (Bogart, 1991; Walsh & Roche, 1979). Yet Walsh and Roche (1979) point out that "such changes are not necessarily pathologic and may reflect in part a heightened sensitivity" (p. 1086).

label: Science & Mathematics
sentence:
Title: Is "intelligent design" a valid scientific concept? (read more)?
Question: Please read this carefully...

Does it rise to the level of a scientific theory?
Or even a hopothesis?
Why or why not?

This link may help:
http://answers.yahoo.com/question/index;_ylt=AtPspx5CqzU_htGM1fYTrRLsy6IX?qid=1006040717662
Answer: No, it really isn't.

The fundamentals of intelligent design are basically anti-science.  The sole argument used in its support is to cease thinking about any subject which is not immediately understood.

"That feature of life looks hard to evolve, therefore, Unnamed Intelligent Designer did it."

I like to look at how history would be different if the great scientists of the past had used such logic.

Isaac Newton:  "Gravity pulls things down, but the moon stays up.  How strange.  Must be God."  (Nobody works out the laws of physical motion.)

Edward Jenner:  "I wonder why milkmaids get smallpox less seriously than other people... Oh, I guess God did it."  (Nobody invents vaccines.)

Intelligent Design "theory" is the death of science.  It is lazy thinking.  It is simply accepting any unknown as an unknown and finding nothing in it worth investigating further.  It is the most fundamentally anti-science idea possible.

Think my examples of overstated?  Consider the real life guru of the ID movement, Michael Behe.  He testified in court that nobody could figure out the evolution of the immune system.  When he was presented with dozens and dozens of articles working out the evolution of the immune system, he admitted having read none of them, but had no compunction about just declaring it "wasn't enough".  How much would be?  Here is a person who has stopped thinking.  He's supposed be a biochemist, but he has no interest in expanding biochemistry.  He found a gap and declared that God filled it and his thoughts stopped there.  Many, many other scientists, unencumbered by the albatross of ID continued to investigate and have expanded our knowledge of the immune system extensively, just so Behe can sit back smugly and declare whatever progress they've made cannot possibly be enough.

I repeat, ID is the death of science.  ID is the most fundamentally anti-science idea possible.

ID "theory" is best stated, "It is absolutely undeniable that someone, somewhere, at some point, did some thing, using some methods, to create life."  That's not a theory.  That hardly qualifies as an idea!  But they can't fill in any of the vapidity.  If they fill in any of the unknowns, it becomes obvious they're trying to force their religion onto the masses.  Therefore, they're stuck with a vague framework of an idea.

If they could fill in bits, they might stumble into a theory that was testable.  If we replace "someone" with "My great grandmother", suddenly, we have an idea we can test.  A false idea, but still a testable one.  My great grandmother has identifiable properties.  We know how much biochemistry she knew.  We can judge the likelihood of her having done such a thing.  That likelihood is, of course, so close to zero there's little point in calculating it.

If we fill in the "how" gap with "using a screwdriver", then again, we can test it.

But ID theory refuses to fill in the gaps.  It claims to not be interested in who.  It claims to not be interested in where, when, how or what.  Dembski says it's a theory of "design detection".  But, again, how do we test it?

Dembski's filter resolves to two states:  Yes, it was designed!  We don't know.

So, can this be falsified?  Can we send something designed through and have the filter produce a false negative?  No, because the filter has no negative state.  It doesn't say "designed/not designed", it says "designed/don't know".  There is no way to test for a false negative.

Can we test for a false positive?  Nope.  Since God is on the table here (and they refuse utterly to let natural laws have sway like real science does), everything in the universe supposedly could be designed.  So there is nothing that you can definitively say isn't designed to run through the filter.

label: Politics & Government
sentence:
Question: Is America, and Democratic nation?
Answer: If you're asking if America is a democratic nation, then the answer is yes.

The United States of America is actually a democratic republic.  It is a democracy, in the fact that there is direct election of representatives.  However, these representatives are the ones that actually make the decisions, the ones that make the laws (hence the Republic).  

A republic is a form of government that has a special "class" or elect that make the governmental decisions (laws, etc) that govern the nation.  In our case, the elect are the representatives and senators at the federal level, as well as your local representatives (state, local) that make the decisions.  

Because these members are elected, then we have a democracy as well.  However, a true democracy would require the votes of everyone on every issue (direct democracy).  It would be a little bit tough with a population of 300 million.

Title: What is Spangdahlem Germany like?
Question: How is it to be statinoed there in the USAF?
Answer: As you know, I've also answered your question about Ramstein; so I'll give you more details for both here -- rather than writing out the same answer twice.

Bottom Line TRUTH: "What you get out of an overseas assignment is a direct measure of what you put into it -- period!"

There are a lot of people who sit around base all day long, and never do anything or go anywhere. If you ask them how they liked their assignment they'll tell you it was terrible because "There's nothing to do." But if you put in nothing, you get nothing -- it's that simple. Now, if you're willing to get out -- there's tons of things to do.

Spangdahlem is almost right on the border with Belgium. There are all sorts of places you can go for a day trip. You can go to Brussels, Amsterdam, Paris. All of these are a few hours away.
The city of Trier, nearby Spang, is the oldest city in Germany, and has old Roman ruins, and great shopping. 

Every base offers language courses to help you integrate. If you're willing to extend the effort, you can learn the language, and do even more. Also, Both Ramstein and Spang offer university courses with the University of Maryland where you can get your education through a Master's Degree.

You can go skiing in the Alps, and visit King Ludwig's castles (AWESOME). You can take tours offered by the base and visit anyplace in europe you want to go: Italy? England? Spain? You name it, there are tours.

Also, there's a company called "Ryanair" that flies out of a nearby commercial airport that offers super-cheap airfares (say -- twenty dollars -- round trip) to London, and to many other locales in Europe. Take advantage of it.

Both Ramstein and Spang have very active Officers' and Enlisted Spouce's organizations. If you want to be involved with base activities and meet new friends, you'll have all the opportunities you want.

You can travel, you can sightsee, you can shop, you can take classes, you can be involved with the community. You can be as involved and active as you wish. That's what I mean when I say, that what you get out of the experience is exactly what you put into it.

Any questions??

==============================================

Spangdahlem is in the Eifel Region of Germany. It's a very little town and a very big base. The closest towns nearby are Bitburg and Trier (the oldest city in Germany). Spang has a fairly high ops tempo, and it's a busy place to be. If you can make your question more specific, I'd be happy to give more details.

Title: Controling my nervousness while presenting a speech?
Question: On this Wednesday, I have to present a speech in front of the whole class. Problem is, I get really nervous when standing in front of a class to present. My English teacher gave us some helpful hints as to not getting shy and nervous in front of the class, but can anyone else explain a bit more thoroughly? Thanks in advance.
Answer: I am a teacher who also gets very nervous when doing a presentation or workshop in front of my peers, so try these tricks:

1) Practice, practice, practice.  Rehearse in front of your family, friends, a mirror, whatever.  The more you know the material, the easier it will come.  Alot of the times you may get nervous because you are afraid you are going to screw up or look silly.  If you have what you are going to say down, that should help.  

2) Before you go up, use the restroom.  On the way there, take big strides and swing your arms steadily.  Your goal here is to burn off the extra adrenaline and rthe exercise will help you relax.

3) I cannot remember the proper name for this technique, but it DOES work.  Breathe in, tighten your stomach muscles, working from the top ones down to the bottom ones.  What you are doing is burning off excess adrenaline and at the same time breathing slower and deeper.  I use this one every time and it works great.  Once you have finished with the bottom muscles, exhale and repeat.

4)  Relax...Breathe in slowly, hold your breath for 4 to 5 seconds, then slowly exhale.

5)  Remember... that nobody sitting there is judging you.  They all understand how nerve racking it can be to speak in public.  They want you to succeed.

6)  Pick one friendly, smiling face in the crowd and focus on that one person.  This doesn't mean that you don't scan the room and present to the class, but always return your focus to that one person and you will be ok.

Hope this helps!

"There are two types of speakers: those that are nervous and those that are liars". - Mark Twain

Title: I like tango, is it too bad for my bad knees?
Question: hey guys, i took a tango class for 1 month( level 1 ). and then 3 months ago got a bad knee injury that has left me with much arthritis. I'm 26. so now wi feel a bit better, although weird and not like i was when normal, but i'm thinking i want to do tango again.. maybe not now, but next year or sometime later, . i've seen salsa and other dances and seems they would be worse for my knees, but one time when i first asked the dance teacher "IS TANGO FOR ME?" she said "If you can walk you can do tango"  NOw after a few months i can walk.. but sometimes it hurts and i limp and feel alot of pain.. soo.. any advice?

You're also not moving at 100 mph, like you can be in Salsa; it's more slow and sensual.  (Well - if you dance tango like they do in some movies like "The Tango Lesson", it can be fast, but that's not the rule.)  There are some patterns like dips that may be more stressful, but you can avoid them, since you're leading. Title: Advice urgently needed about withdrawal from triclyclic antidepressant,, extreme neck pain ?

I am fine emotionally and mentally, however the extrem neck pain is really upsetting and disrupting my life (I have two young kids, though my bloke does help !).  I know upper neck and jaw pain is a common w/d symptom, I can cope if it is just short term but have tried every legal possible painkiller and it doenst change. this is third day (and night). I can't sleep for the pain.  Can anyone advise. ?
Answer: I can only advise from my own experience.  Please tell your doctor that you think you need a muscle relaxant for a little while until this neck pain goes away.  Just ask to take one at bedtime because they might make you drowsy.  

Since this is neck and jaw pain, you are probably also a person who grits their teeth at night.  You need to relax.  If you don't mind my suggestions, there are different types of non prescription medications such a Benadryl that you can take at night to help you relax, but I would check with your doctor for a muscle relaxant.  

I am so sorry you are having this problem.  It sounds more to me like anxiety than anything else.  Either that, or you may be developing arthritis in your neck in which case you also need something to relax.    

BE sure and check with your doctor, this could be more than withdrawal.  I suffered with this until it got so bad, I could not turn my neck at all.  I kept taking Ibuprofen constantly and it did not help at all. Just made me feel funny in the head.  Finally, I found I had arthritis in my neck as well as some spurs that had formed on my neck that were pressing on my nerves.  I was given some medication that helped out a lot and I don't know your names in the UK but your doctor can help you with this.  Do you have chiropractic medicine where you live? Best wishes.
