Title: Is the NTRP (National Tennis Rating Program) effective at categorizing tennis players?
Question: Does the NTRP, as currently offered by the USTA, categorize tennis players accurately and make competition fair between players? Or, is the NTRP ineffective and require overhaul?

jeffspin@comcast.net
Answer: Good question. Unfortunately, there are very mixed motives involved in the current classification system. Those who play in leagues or tournaments usually want the lowest rating they can get so they can win. Those who use the rating to let others know how good they are, usually want to be rated higher.
If you are "accurately" rated, you will likely be mismatched against those who fudge. This encourages a downward push such that those who previously might have been 5.0s, for example, are now 4.5s.
Ratings now appear to be based first on your self-assessment, which is frequently falsified, and secondly on your results. I know that players will lose a few matches on purpose just to avoid being moved up a level. This clearly is not in the best interests of the game or in fair competition.
So, I do not believe the system is effective in accurately classifying players.

Answer: V = πr²h
A (top & bottom) = πr²
End Area = 2πr²
Lateral Area = 2πrh
Cost of tube = 2πrhC, C being cost per unit area
Cost of ends = 2πr²C*1.2
Total cost, P = 2πC(1.2r² + rh)
h = V/πr², so

P = 2πC(1.2r² + V/πr)
dP/dr = 2πC(2.4r - V/πr²) = 0 for max or min, so

r³ = V/2.4π
r³ = 5/2.4π

Question: Calculate the molecular mass:8.02g of solute in 861g of water lower the freezing point to -0.430c?
Answer: O.k., so you are given the final temperature (-0.430 C). Since the freezing point of water is usually O degrees C, the temperature decrease is 0.43 degrees C. Like in the other problem, let's set up some dimensional analysis.

(0.43 deg.C decr)*(1 mole compound / 1.86 deg.C decr) = X

Here X would equal 0.23 moles compound

Next, you want to find the grams of solute in solution.

(8.02g solute/0.861 kg solvent) = Y

Y here is equal to 9.31 g compound/kg solution

Now that you have the mass in grams and the number of moles of the solute, you can divide Y by X, which gives the units for molecular mass (g/ mol.)

The answer should be around 40.48 g/mol. The solute cannot be determined from this information because no additional information is given concerning what is most likely a compound (not a pure element).

sentence:
Title: Veryfing trigonometric identities.?
Question: I am having trouble to prove that:

a) Tan X - Csc X Sec X (1 - 2 cos^2 X) = cot X

b) (Sin X + Tan X)/(Cot X + Csc X) = Sin X * Tan X

What I tried to do in both of them was:
For a)

Tan X - Csc X Sec X * 1 - cos^2 X - cos^2 X =
Tan X - Csc X Sec X * Sin^2 X - Cos^2 X =
Tan X - Csc X Sec X 
And I don't know what to do after that.

For b)
(Sin X + Sin X/Cos X) / (Cos X /Sin X+ 1/Sin X) =
[(Sin X*Cos X+ Sin X) / Cos X] / [(Cos X +1)/Sin X] =
(Sin^2 X + Sin^2 X* Cos X) / Sin^2 X
Stuck after that.

I'd really appreciate any suggestions on how to solve this ones, or tips for getting quicker to the solution. Having a bad time with them. Thanks.
Answer: For the first one, let's first rewrite "cscx secx" as "1 / (sinx cosx)"

So we have:

tanx - (1-2cos²x)/(sinx cosx) =

tanx + (2cos²x - 1)/(sinx cosx) =

(sinx/cosx) + (2cos²x - 1)/(sinx cosx) =

(sin²x/sinx cosx) + (2cos²x - 1)/(sinx cosx) =

(sin²x + cos²x + cos²x - 1)/(sinx cosx) =

(1 + cos²x - 1)/(sinx cosx) =

cos²x / (sinx cosx) =

cosx/sinx = cotx

~ ~ ~ ~ 

For the second one, you started off in the right direction!  Let's do it here:

( sinx + tanx ) / (cotx + cscx) = 

( sinx + sinx/cosx) / (cosx/sinx + 1/sinx) = 

( (sinxcosx + sinx) / cosx ) * ( sinx / (1 + cosx)) =

-- now I'm just going to rearrange the terms a bit --

( (sinxcosx + sinx) / (1 + cosx ) * ( sinx / cosx ) =

( sinx(1+cosx) / (1+cosx) ) * sinx/cosx = 

sinx * tanx

~ ~ ~ ~

Tips for solving -- experience, trial and error (sorry that's not too helpful!).   What I did for the second one was I started out like you did, then I rewrote where I wanted to end up (sinx tanx) as sinx * sinx/cosx to see if I could manipulate where I had gotten so far with my problem to where I wanted to go, and I was able to see how to connect the two.  Hope that helps somewhat.  I had a hard time with trig identities when I first learned them too.  They really just take lots and lots of practice.

label: Science & Mathematics
sentence:
Question: why does pubic hair grow to a certain length and then stop?
Answer: There are a lot of kinds of "hair". Each species of mammal has at least one kind of "hair" or fur. Many species have several different specialized types. For example, cat whiskers are very different from regular cat fur in texture and length. One of the main differences in hair is whether it is determinate in length (grows to a certain length and stops) or indeterminate in length (grows for as long as it is alive.) Humans have both kinds in different places on the body. Head hair, scalp and face, is indeterminate. Body hair, arms, underarms, legs, pubic area, fingers and toes is determinate. The only determinate hairs on the head are normal eyebrows, ear hair and nose hairs. I think the reason is obvious. "Wild hairs" are determinate hairs that have encountered a genetic failure. The length possibilities of each type of hair from sheep's wool to seal fur are genetically determined.  Pubic hair is a secondary sex characteristic that signals availability for mating. It is not designed to cover, conceal, protect, or warm the area that produces it. It may have some scent retaining or focusing function too. This is still debatable. I hope this helps.

Title: A question related to PHP and SQL and all that good stuff...?
Question: Ooooook,

Say I have a table in a database that has several entries. Each entry is a message between users. There are fields like "tousername" and "fromusername" in the table. I'd like to set up a page that would list the current 'conversations' between the user viewing the page and the other users talking to him.

So assuming I select * from the table where the "tousername" equals the user viewing the page, since there are multiple messages to this user from the same person, if I just used a "while()" it would list each entry so every message would show up on this page. I'd like to find a way to select the data from the table but only once for each identical "fromusername", if that makes sense. So that way, each 'conversation' would only appear once on the page and you could see a list of users that you were currently having a conversation with, but without duplicate users because of each row in the table.

Thanks. :p
Answer: SELECT fromusername, tousername
FROM table
GROUP BY tousername, fromusername
HAVING fromusername = 'name of user'
AND status = 'open'

Assuming you have a column, named status, that indicates which conversations are active. That will bring in only the unique pairs you describe.

As described earlier, you could also use DISTINCT:

SELECT DISTINCT tousername, fromusername
FROM table
WHERE fromusername = 'name of user'
AND status = 'open'

The GROUP BY statement is computationally more efficient, but unless you are dealing with millions of records and thousands of concurrent requests, you shouldn't see a difference in performance.

Title: What qualities make a great goaltender?
Question: Like Roy - what made him the greatest (IMO)?  Or Hasek or Brodeur or even Miller...?  Is it stance, leadership, size, "je ne se qua"...?
Answer: I think every goalie has his or her own winning combination -- some of them are brainy like Roy or Shields, some are huge and massive and forwards fear them like Brodeur, some are unbelievably quick and nimble and weirdly preternatural in a scary "spidey sense" way about the puck.  Nabby was that way for a while, Toskala now.

Like any other position, I think the best goalies reinvent the game at their level.  They own the plays, the net, their role on the team, and I don't think that necessarily amounts to leadership, but it does come from things like maturity and a certain solid footing.  Um, no pun intended.

I think some of the things I look for in a goalie I play with in rec are similar in pro hockey.  I don't like goalies who fall apart after letting one or two in, or goalies who are inflexible in their approach, which means they can only shut out certain teams and only if we defend a certain way in front of them.

I like playing with goalies who are fluid about the game, not prima donnas, who can clear their own crease if they have to and who can and will drive the game from the net if the situation warrants it.  Goaltending isn't for the fainthearted, and there's some wussy goalies out there.  I don't think, long term rec or pro, they do very well.

I was sad to see Shields go so completely downhill.  He was amazing to watch when he was at his best, and I wish he'd seen his full potential.  I'm watching Aebischer and Toskala now, of the new generation.  Then again, I know jack about goalies except for living with one.  

They have too much expensive gear and they leave it lying around all over the !@#!!! house.  That's my opinion on goalies.  How's that?  :p

label: Science & Mathematics
sentence:
Question: how do i keep grackles out of my birdfeeders?
Answer: Try some of these suggestions:

1. Place a variety of feeders in your yard, including "thistle" feeders and suet feeders.

2. Put a cage or screen around your seed feeders so only smaller birds can get to the food. Build your own using chicken wire or buy one of the commercial bird feeders made especially to solve this problem.

3. Use a Hopper type feeder with a weighted perch that closes when a heavy bird (or squirrel) lands on it.

4. Keep bird seed off the ground and stop filling your platform feeder for a week. Blackbirds and Starlings may get discouraged and move on.

5. Shorten the perches on your tube feeders. The smaller birds (Goldfinches, Chickadees and Titmice) will be able to eat but larger birds will not be able to land.

6. If Starlings are eating all your suet, try a feeder that required the birds to hang upside down. Woodpeckers can eat like that, but Starlings hate it.

7. Never buy seed mixes containing milo. Blackbirds are the only birds that seem to like milo! Blackbirds also like millet and cracked corn, but few of the colorful songbirds eat these seeds. You might try offering safflower seeds instead of sunflower seeds in your tube feeders.

label: Health
sentence:
Title: I want to start off on my birthday by becoming healthy...but I have no idea where to start!  If you have ever?
Question: made a change to your diet and fitness, please help!!!!

I've tried contacting a dietitian on Craigs List, but he kept promoting some box drinks...I want to learn HOW to eat properly, not be fed something that supposedly IS healthy.

FOr instance, what is a healthy breakfast?
How do you stave off hunger?

Is it best to withdraw from food at the beginning (like a fast) to prepare your system?

Pls advise....
Answer: A healthy diet consists of a variety of food groups....let me be specific. Lets say you are a female (which I think you are) with a moderate activity level, for example: exercise 3 times a week for 45 min. or 5 times a week for 20 mins. This includes stretching 4 times a week and some sort of strength training (this could be as simple as carrying groceries for a few blocks or actually weight lifting) once or twicw weekly. It is recommended (Canada's food guide) that you eat 1900-2200 calories per day. ;Broken down even further, the food guide suggests:
7 fruits/vegetables
7 grains
3 dairy products
2 meat/alternatives
6 fats (1 fat serving is every 5g of extra oil, butter, you get the picture)
This combination of food equals roughly 2000 cal. (try not to get caught up in the numbers, this will only make you crazy)
Also, try eating this combination of food in the form of 3 meals and 3 snacks. Every meal and snack should consist of a carbohydrate source (such as fruit/vegetables, grains) and a protein source (dairy or meat). This combination helps you to feel full and satisfied (as well as keeps your metabolism working) throughout the day. Try aiming for 2 food groups for snacks and at least three food groups for meals. Always try to eat breakfast within the first half hour of waking up then have a snack about 2 and a half hours later, then lunch 2 and a half hours later then.....you get it, this way until bed time snack. I don't advise withdrawing from food to begin with your body is always prepared to be treated well :-).
Hope this helps, it can be time consuming but in the end you will feel better then you ever have and your body thanks you for it.
Good luck and happy birthday!

sentence:
Title: Planning a Christmas theme wedding?
Question: Am helping a friend plan a Christmas theme wedding for next year. What details and touches would you incorporate?\n\nThey are having the ceremony at the reception site.
Answer: We planned our wedding, in six weeks, for the week before Christmas.  We also had the ceremony at the reception site.  First, you should see if the site will already be decorating for the holidays.  Ours did and it saved us so much money.  We served Roast Beef and Chicken family style (trays were brought to the tables and people served themselves).  The guys wore silver vests and the girls wore apple red.  Our cake was white with a silver ribbon wrapped around it.  For our wedding favors I purchased 150 small silver bells with hearts on the top that also doubled as placecard holders.  We also had a friend bake us gingerbread men and woman and "dressed" them up with tuxes and dresses (using basic frosting).  The bells were perfect for those guests who are obsessed with having the bride and groom kiss every ten seconds!  I think it would be a great idea to do a christmas theme.  It always seems to put people in great spirits and we got some amazing pictures in front of the decorated christmas tree.

Question: How can I find a mentor or someone to invest in my idea for a business as well as a loan to start one?
Answer: First, I hope you have a formal business plan on paper.  You can go to the SBA about a loan at http://www.sba.gov, or if you live in a fiar sized city, there may be a local sba. Traditional banks will consider loaning too, but they will expect you to pony up or raise a lot of the cash on your own.

As far as other to invest in your business, I think you may be looking for a venture capitalist or "angel."  A venture capital firm or angel investor can provide you with startup monies, but it is usually an investment, not a loan, which means they would own a portion of your business, be able to sell their part, and have their say in how you run it.  Have a look at http://www.vfinance.com/

A third option would be a grant....if you are a woman or minority, these are fairly common....just search on Yahoo here for small business grant woman or small business grant <<<insert race here>>>.

Best of luck!  My wife and I went through this a few years back, and it can be a real hassle, but work and persistence in searching for start up $$$ can creat great results!

Title: math problem, vapor pressures?
Question: Small quantities of oxygen gas are sometimes generated by heating   KClO3   in the presence of   MnO2   as a catalyst:


        2KClO3(s)   →   2KCl(s)   +   3O2(g)


What volume (ml) of   O2   is collected over water at   24.0   oC   by the reaction of   0.275 g   of   KClO3   if the barometric pressure is   727.5 mm Hg  
The vapor pressure of water at   24.0 oC   is   22.4 mm Hg.
Answer: To answer this, you can use the ideal gas law, V = nRT/P

You know R , T  and P, andso you need to find n.

To find n , note that 2 moles of KClO3 produces 3 moles of O2. Given the mass of KClO3, you kind find the moles of this compound by dividing the mass by the molar mass. Assuming that there is 100% conversion, you can use the ration above to find the moles of O2.

Lastly, I'm not sure, but I think you need to use the gage pressure, which is the barometric pressure - the vapor pressure.

Title: Delphi Indy TCP Client / Server send recive Files using latest version 10. >?
Question: Hi, i am new to using Indy and is trying to create a simple client server chat program and need to add file transfer to it so fare no luck with it any demo/ advice would be appreiated thank
Answer: I've used the Indy 8 and 9.  The standard TIdTCPServer component should suffice to build a simple chat application.  The client application would use the TIdTCPClient component.  The most direct method is to work out some standard commands, and assign them to the server's CommandHandlers property.  It would also be useful to work out some standard response codes so the client knows what the server is doing.

When chat messages are sent (for example through a SendCmd call to TIdTCPClient), you simply have the CommandHandler on the server read the incoming text (OnCommand for the CommandHandler) the iterate the clients (TIdTCPServer.Bindings) and Write the text to the connections.  The clients can periodically call ReadLn (during a timer event) to check to see if the server sent any chat messages.

Things to keep in mind:
On the server, each client connects using it's own thread, so you have to have some familiarity with thread synchronization.

If you're planning to use the chat server over the Internet, you should have a cursory understanding of how firewalls work (e.g. port blocking) in case clients can't connect to your server.

Ultimately, there should be some examples in you Indy install directory or in your Delphi demos directory.

Enjoy!

Hope this helps.

label: Education & Reference

Title: Inclusion for Special Education?
Question: Does anyone have any information on inclusion for special education students (websites, personal experiences, etc...)
Answer: Inclusion is when students with a need for individiualized instruction are included in the regular classroom and receive the services they need within the classroom setting.  This may be for some or all classes.

Students who are mainstreamed are most often students with mild to moderate learning or emotional disabilities.  They will have an invoiivualized education plan (IEP) written by a team of people concerned about his/her educational progress.  That team generally incudes special education teacher, regular education teachers, specialists such as speech therapists, parents and representatives from any community service providing agencies.

The IEP will include modifications and accomodations that may be made within the general education setting to allow the student to thrive.  These may be as simple as untimed tests and seating near the teacher, to having the teacher wear a special sound ampligfication device, among others.

Does inclusion work?  Well, that depends on the school district's commitment to inclduing kids in the regular classroom, on the students (and parents') willingness to meet some general classroom expectations, and upon the skill of the classroom teacher.  If everyone works together and expects success, it generally happens.  If any member of the instructional team doubts the child's ability to succedd, it usually becomes a self-fulfilling prohecy, and the child may end up back in a separate special education setting. This special environment is viewed as being a more restictive environment, whereas the incluusion class is viewed as a less restrictive environment, as required by the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA).

My third grader has surprised some naysayers and has been included in regular education for math and special subjects for two years now.  I also enjoy helping students reach their academic goals.

I hope this answers your question.

Title: Can blind people see their dreams?

People who are visually impaired from birth appear to lack visual imagery in their dreams. It's believed that the parts of their brains that register visual information remain dormant. 
According to this fascinating article by Diego Kaski in the International Medical Students' Journal, even people who lose their sight early in childhood retain visual imagery in their dreams well into adulthood. However, this imagery fades over time. 

Nevertheless, blind people do dream and often describe their dreams in terms of places and surroundings. An article from the University of Santa Cruz notes that blind dreams feature a "very high percentage of gustatory, olfactory, and tactual sensory references," something very unusual for sighted dreamers to experience.

sentence:
Title: When standing, blood pressure in your legs is greater than in your upper body.?
Question: Would this be true for an astronaut in orbit?
Answer: Normally the systolic pressure in the legs is upto 20 mmHg higher than in the arms, but the diastolic pressures are virtually identical. 


To be able to explore and work in space, humans have to take their environment with them because there is no atmosphere to supply the pressure and oxygen necessary to support life. Without sufficient atmospheric pressure, body fluids will start to heat up and boil. Without oxygen, we would be unable to breathe. 
The parts of a spacesuit

Spacesuits serve many functions. Today's spacesuits are pressurized, have an oxygen supply, protect the astronaut from micrometeoroid bombardment while spacewalking, and insulate the astronaut from the severe temperature changes experienced in space. The Space Shuttle astronauts have more than one "outfit" for space travel. What they wear while on a mission is determined by the job they are doing. During the launch and re-entry, the astronauts wear a partially pressurized suit and a parachute pack. The suit has a helmet, gloves, and boots which all serve as protection for the astronaut. Within the suit are bladders that automatically fill with air at reduced cabin pressures. At low pressure, the blood will pool in the lower body causing the astronaut to black out. The bladders maintain the pressure on the lower body to prevent this from happening. While working in the Shuttle during orbit, astronauts work in comfortable clothes such as knit shirts, pants, or flight suits. In addition, prior to each mission, flight crews are outfitted with lined jackets, sleep shorts, slippers, and underwear. 
While working outside of the Shuttle during a mission, astronauts wear an extravehicular mobility unit (EMU). This suit has interchangeable parts so it can be assembled to fit different astronauts. This makes the suit more cost effective since it can be reused. The EMU has a liquid cooling garment, which is a one piece suit made of spandex, and keeps the astronaut cool while in the suit. The unit also contains headphones and microphones, a drink bag which carries water, a life support system containing oxygen, and a urine collection device. Gloves are included with the unit along with a helmet and a visor. All of this is necessary to protect the astronaut from micrometeoroids, solar radiation, infrared radiation, temperature changes, pressure changes, and oxygen deprivation.

Title: N-Acetyl Cysteine and N-Acetyl-L-Cysteine.?
Question: What is the difference between N-Acetyl cysteine and N-Acetyl L Cysteine?
I use N-Acetyl cysteine as a supplement and a mucolitic for my sinus. Will N-Acetyl L cysteine better or the same or worse?
Answer: They are really the same thing.  

N-Acetyl Cysteine is the general name of the compound.  The compound, like all amino acids, exists in two optical isomers: the L-isomer and the D-isomer form.  the L-isomer is the most common form found in the proteins of living organisms.  The two forms are basically identical with respect to ordinary chemical reactions.
N-Acetyl-L-Cysteine is commonly reported as N-Acetyl-Cysteine, without the "-L-".  
So, there shouldn't be any difference between the two.
N-Acetyl-L-Cysteine is the more precise chemical name.

label: Sports
sentence:
Question: What do you think of this televised Olypmics?
Answer: I remember back in 1984 being enthralled by the Olympics in Los Angeles. Every night for two weeks, my family was glued to the set to get the updates from the day's events.  We didn't have to watch 8- to 10-hours of coverage to see who won. All we had to do was wait until prime-time and we could see in one hour who the big winners were, and then spend another one or two hours watching a live event.

Now, 20 years later, around-the-clock coverage is given on no fewer than 10 stations, not counting the foreign language presentations.  The updates my family got when I was a kid are only given briefly on the fly from one event to another.

I feel overwhelmed with all of the coverage. It feels like the covering network has placed that much coverage to fit in all the big-name sponsors and to sell their shows.  Granted, if it weren't for this type of coverage, we wouldn't see some of the more unusual events, like curling, which in the past were treated as more of a side-bar of the games.  But the complete onslaught of the games is a bit much.

Title: please help me?
Question: Two point-source loudspeakers are a certain distance apart, and a person stands 12.0 m in front of one of them on a line perpendicular to the baseline of the speakers. If the speakers emit identical 1000.0-Hz tones, what is their minimum nonzero separation so that the observer hears little or no sound? (Take the speed to be exactly 340 m/s.)
Answer: Ley y be the non zero seperation. Then minimum nonzero separation so that the observer hears little or no sound is given by  
            y = {(2n+1)vD}/2fd 
where v = 340 m/s
      D = 12 m
      d = distance b/w loud speakers
      f = 1000 Hz

Take n = 0

      y = 2.04/d m ( here d is not given)

sentence:
Title: What made the building of the Panama canal an almost impossible feat?
Question: A. How were the obstacles elliminated?


B. Why was the completion of this massive project which took ten years to build such a big deal when it finally opened?
Answer: A. Various diseases hampered the construction project because many people died.  Yellow fever and Malaria were the most deadly of them, because before the cause of them was discovered (mosquitoes) they didn't know how to treat the disease.

Also the original French plan called for a sea level canal like Suez.  Unfortunately for the French the Panamanian landscape didn't allow them to dig so easily as they did in Suez, and the technology they were using in Panama was the same one as they used in Suez, which was all wrong.

When the US got the rights to build the canal arising from the Hay - Buneau Varilla treat of 1903, they reengineered the plans and decided to go for a lock type canal, rather than a sea level canal.  They based this on a prior study from a French engineer.  They also brought new technology with them, for example Concrete.  Remember we're talking about 1903 here.

Also the US got a hold of the research that a Cuban medic called Carlos Finlay did on Yellow Fever where he discovered that mosquitoes were the vectors causing the disease, and the incubation time needed for the mosquitoes to transfer the disease.

With that the US drained swamps, and they fumigated the entire Canal Zone, along with the Panamanian Cities of Cristobal, Colon and Panama to get rid of the mosquitoes.

B. Actually it wasn't a big deal when the Canal opened in 1914.  It was the smallest story on the front page news.  Remember WWI just broke out in Europe, so the news from the battlefront were more interesting than the first transit of the canal.  By the way it was done by the Steamship Ancon.

Now regarding commerce and the military advantage it gave the US, it was a big deal.  Ships could now shorten the time it took them to go around the Cape of Horns in South America, and also for those ships that had to cross the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa.  The US military could complement their fleets just crossing some vessels through the Canal.  Think about all the savings it brought to commerce, and the possibilites to the military strategists at that time.

Also until 1977 the Panama Canal was controlled by the US Military, not the US Federal Government as some still think.  The office handling the Panama Canal affairs was in the Pentagon, not the Secretary of Commerce.  After 1977 with the new Panama Canal Treaties (they were 3 treaties in one single body) The Neutrality Treaty declared the Panama Canal neutral in all times of wars and crisis, therefore now any ship couldn't be denied the right to go through the Panama Canal.  Although I don't believe that prior to 1977 the US actually denied transit except in WWII for obvious reasons.

Title: This is about child support! I really need help?
Question: I looked up to see if my ex- boyfriend had a warrant for child support. It said he had a civil attachment issued in 2005 what does that mean??? HELP!! Is this a warrant or not? any info will help.
Answer: Former police officer/current attorney...working in child support.

A civil attachment is similar to an arrest warrant, but then again it isn't.

Its probably where the Judge wants to speak with your boyfriend about his child support obligation. Sadly, alot of times you can't get the fathers to voluntarily come in and see the Judge. So, they issue these attachments. More than likely your boyfriend didn't live up to his part of the bargain. I would recommend he get it taken care of...it can turn into a criminal matter. He'll probably have to go before the Judge. The Judge will ask some questions, maybe put some restrictions on him as far as his support. Nothing too serious, but like I said IT CAN turn serious...

Its not really a "criminal charge", but attachments are usually served by law enforcement. He won't have any criminal record from a civil order. Good luck.

Title: I have a pimple on my chin, big! but it isn't like a pimple, its like a inside lump.swollen it did go now?
Question: but, i thought it was a spider bit but i dont think so,its like ingrow,big lump. , have u ever got this?? 
, what should i do to make it go away ,,,fast...how did i get this!!!!!!
Answer: Okay there are several possibilities here.  One is cystic acne, HOWEVER, if you have not had cystic acne before it would be very unusual for it to start now and for you to have only one spot effected! (fyi, cystic acne is aka underground pimples and do not come to a "head" easily and often leave scars).  Two, this could be an ingrown hair. This is much more common in males who shave but can occur in females as well. The hair literally has been covered with epidermis (top layer of skin) and is growing inward which causes a local inflammatory reaction/infection.  Third, an abscess caused by a local infection.  Now, to be technically correct all of the above, including a basic pimple, are abscesses (pus filled lesions). I am differentiating by cause be it a cystic pimple, ingrown hair or secondary infection (i.e. a scratch).

Treatment: "Let the 'evil' humours out!" 
In other words..."release the pus!"  Most teenagers are adept at this by squeezing their 'zits,' but the type of lesion/lump you have will not simply erupt with squeezing. If anything, you risk making it worse! So what do you do? Well, you can try: 
1) Direct heat with a wash cloth soaked in the hottest water you can stand without burning yourself and an astringent such as Witch Hazel.  This will, hopefully, bring the lesion to a 'head' (a whitish or thin dome on top) at which point it is ready for extruding (i.e. a good squeeze to release the pus)!) 2) Apply antibiotic cream or ointment 3 times a day along with a secondary antibiotic like Oxy 10 (this will hopefully reduce the size by fighting the infection). 3) Finally, IF the lump is indeed pus filled and not simple induration (inflammatory response that precedes the pus stage) you need it drained. IF you are lucky and step number one allowed you to get rid of the pus (that white/yellow nasty stuff that you get out of pimples) then, Great! BUT, if you have an ingrown hair or the secondary infection then you will need 'surgical' drainage and treatment of the underlying problem. In other words, a doctor needs to lance the lump with a scalpel. DON'T STRESS! This is done with a bit of local anesthetic and a quick stab with a small surgical blade which releases the pus and you instantly feel much better! You may need oral antibiotics such as cephalexin or sulfa or clindamycin or doxicycline as well as topical (skin applied) antibiotics to treat the infection. The doctor may remove the ingrown hair if that is the cause.

Bottom line: IF the lump does NOT come to a head or does not recede with topical treatment then you need to see your doctor for definitive care. Don't stress! The treatment is FAR better than the alternative of a worsened infection that could, RARELY, lead to admission to the hospital for major IV antibiotics and surgery.  Treat it early and aggressively!

ALSO, Since I know that people with pimples may be reading this...PLEASE be careful in squeezing pimples in the 'T' zone. This is the area from the tip of your nose to the forehead from between your eyebrows! The drainage system of this area leads DIRECTLY toward your brain!  I am not joking in relating the following anecdote: I had a patient DIE of a pimple! He squeezed one in this T zone and the infection spread to his brain and he died of cerebritis (brain infection) despite aggressive treatment!

USE topical antibiotics or see your doctor if you have a 'zit' that gets bigger in this 'T' Zone or has worsened redness of the surrounding skin (aka Cellulitis).

Good Luck!

Greg M.D.

Title: Why are so many people obsessed on downloading free software?
Question: I never understand the desire of people to steal things.  Free music, free movies, free software, free games.  Limewire, Emule, Bit Torrent, Kazaa, the original Napster.  Why do so many people feel it is their right to steal the work of others?

Why does stealing music on-line seem ok, but stealing a CD or DVD from a store still seem bad?

Are we all to cheap to buy something, or are we all just closet thieves, and the internet lets some of us do it in a more safe manner?
Answer: The real answer is that copying software and music or movies is not stealing. It is copyright infringement, which is not a criminal offense. Stealing a CD or DVD from a store is actually stealing. It is a criminal offense. Stealing a CD deprives the artist, store owner, and label of the profit that they would have gotten by selling the CD. Copying music and downloading the file only deprives them of money if the person downloading would have purchased the music otherwise, which is almost never the case.

So don't equate copyright infringement with stealing, because it is a much lesser offense. The music industry likes to use the terms "stealing," "piracy," and "theft," because it uses language to subconsciously alter how people are thinking about the problem. Don't fall into that trap.

That said, copyright infringement *is* a civil offense that is illegal. I don't think people are closet thieves, I just think that the actual value of the products that these people are producing is far less than the cost, and people feel justified in downloading it because they feel somewhat overcharged for the music they do purchase.

Title: If a Catholic is a Christian, why do they differentiate themselves?
Question: I've asked several of my friends are you Catholic or Christian, they will either say "we are Christian" or "we are Catholic".  When I ask them what is the difference, they said " Catholic believes in Virgin Mary and Christian does not".  Can you list out what's the difference and who they worship?  I checked online and didn't give me such 
explanation.  Thank you very much.
Answer: We believe in the apostolic authority of the pope and the pope's infalibility in matters of faith and morals. People mess this up and say we worship the pope or believe he can't sin.

We believe that the Blessed Virgin Mary is to be honored above all other humans (except Jesus), and that she is the Mother of God incarnate. We ask her to intercede for us, just like you'd ask your best friend to pray for you. People misinterpret this and say we worship her. We worship God alone in the Blessed Trinity.

We believe that Jesus Christ instituted seven sacraments, or visible signs through which He gives us grace. All seven are biblical. (See http://biblechristiansociety.com and http://catholic.com for more information.)

Probably one of the most central doctrines of our faith (Protestants reconize this as well) is the Real Presence of Christ in the Eucharist. Catholics take the Last Supper and John 6 literally. We believe the bread and wine becomes Jesus' Body and Blood under the appearances of Bread and wine.

We believe in salvation by God's grace alone. Not by faith alone, and not by works alone. We need faith and works, or faith working through love, as St. Paul puts it.

We also do not believe in sola scriptura, or scripture alone. We believe that Jesus left a Church to guide us (Mt. 16: 18-19) and that we need Sacred Traditon as well.

These are only parts of our beautiful faith. To learn more, see the websites mentioned above, as well as 

http://www.usccb.org/catechism/text/

which is an online Catechism and holds everything Catholics believe.

To sum it up though,

http://www.creeds.net/ancient/nicene.htm

This is the Nicene Creed which we say at each Mass as a congregation.

God Bless, hope this helps...

A devoted Catholic Christian.

label: Politics & Government
sentence:
Question: what is dmk?
Answer: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) is a regional political party in the Tamil Nadu state of India. It was founded by C N Annadurai as a breakaway faction from Dravidar Kazhagam, headed by Periyar. The party is currently headed by M Karunanidhi, the former Chief Minister of the state.

The movement was initially mooted as one that championed the cause of socially and economically disadvantaged sections of the society. It advocated concepts of rationality, self-respect and rejection of casteism and superstitious practices, prevalent in the Tamil society. Prominent members preached militant atheism. The movement was sympathetic to the claim that there were two separate races in India, the Aryans and Dravidians, and the movement claimed to represent the latter. In the early years of its militant struggle, it rejected any concept known to have its origins in the north. There also was a brief period, during which it idealized a separate Dravidian land, comprising the southern regions of India, and Tamil Eelam. The anti-Hindi agitation of 1965, forced the central government to abandon its efforts to stipulate Hindi as the only official language of the country. With the passage of time and a shift in the national political scenario towards coalition governments, however, DMK has adopted a more national outlook. DMK championed the cause of Tamil and used its national clout to make Government of India declare Tamil as classical language. In the enrichment of Tamil literature, the writers belonging to DMK had an important role, although it needs to be pointed out that their contributions have tended to be more of expressions of dissent and disgruntlement at what was perceived as social injustice and domination of certain communities, in the social sphere, and of the Northern parts of India, in the political sphere, and substitution of less often used Tamil words for borrowed-assimilated popular ones for administrative and oratorical purposes, in the linguistic sphere. The 'contributions' pertain to a short period of a few decades and hence their value will need to be evaluated meaningfully only after several more decades, and that only if the contributions evolve additional dimensions of the ethos of linguistic expression that can be compared to those of earlier eras that have truly enriched the Tamil linguistic and literary heritage in a distinct and ever-lasting manner that caters to the innermost spiritual and intellectual needs of not only the upper strata but also the common man in general. The contributions thus far have centered around the party's campaigns for realizing and maintaining political power at a regional (Tamilnadu) level and in central government.

The DMK is also sympathetic and formerly allied to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam in Sri Lanka.

The DMK has split into the [[AIADMK] and the MDMK. Of this, the AIADMK is the strongest rival party.

Question: what is the difference between a pirate and a buccaneer?
Answer: All buccaneers are pirates but not all pirates are buccaneers. The term buccaneer is used to describe only those pirates who operated in the Caribbean..

Buccaneer is a term that was used in the later 17th century in the Caribbean Islands. The term Buccaneer comes from the French word "Boucanier". These Boucaniers originally were hunters who were poaching cattle and pigs. They would smoke the meat on wooden frames, "boucans", so that it could be saved for a later time. The Boucaniers were taught this by the local Arawak tribes from Santo Domingo, calling the method Barbicoa - which is where the word and method of Barbecue originated.

However, Islanders soon began to use the term buccaneer as a way to describe pirates in the Caribbean during the 1660s. English settlers occupying Jamaica began to spread the name with the meaning of rebel pirates sailing in the Caribbean ports and seas

a brown squirrle can carry a maximum 2 acorns at a time

how many different ways could three squirrles devide up 24 acorns and not leave any left over? each much carry there maximum load.


Question 2,

a brown squirrle can carry a maximum 2 acorns at a time
a gray squirrle can carry a maximum 3 acorns at a time
a black squirrle can carry a maximum 5 acorns at a time

The squirrles realize that they can carry less than there maximum load. how many different ways could the squirrles devide up to 24



I know it is alot to ask 'cause it is sorta 2 questions, but if you answer asap i will give you the best answer!

p.s. i know that there are at least 35 different ways when the squirrles dont carry there maximum load, i also know that there are at least 8 different ways when they do
Answer: Squirrels are carrying maximum acorns gives you following possibilities:

5,5,5,5,2,2:  or 4 trips by black squirrel, 2 by brown
5,5,5,3,2,2,2:  or 3 trips by black squirrel, 1 by gray, 3 by brown
5,5,3,2,3,2,2,2:  or 2 trips by black squirrel, 2 by gray, 4 by brown
5,3,2,3,2,3,2,2,2:  or 1 trip by black squirrel, 3 by gray, 5 by brown
3,2,3,2,3,2,3,2,2,2:  or 4 trips by gray squirrel, 6 by brown
2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2:  or 12 trips by brown squirrel
3,3,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2:  or 2 trips by gray squirrel, 9 by brown

5,5,2,2,2,2,2,2,2:  or 2 trips by black squirrel, 7 by brown
5,5,3,3,3,3,2:  or 2 trips by black squirrel, 4 by gray, 1 by brown

brown = 0, gray = 0, black = 24

brown = 1, gray = 0, black = 23
...etc...

which can be reduced down to the mathematical equation:

1+2+3+4+...+25 = 325 different combinations!

Title: Where does the date and TIME stamp come from when you send an e-mail?
Question: In the header of the e-mail where does the Date and Time come from?  It never comes close to my computer date/time.
Answer: The "Date:" part of the message header does come from the email client. If you're using a web service to send email (like Hotmail or Yahoo mail) it will most likely reflect the time at the server itself and not from your pc.  (This may be where you're getting vastly different times reflected.)

If you're using an SMTP/POP service through Outlook or other non-web mail client, you should get something approximating your local pc time with a time zone indicator after the timestamp, like -0500 for U.S. Eastern, etc.

Hope that helps.

label: Health
sentence:
Title: how do I get post-operative swelling to reduce without perscription drugs???
Question: My daughter has had cochlear implant surgery and is unable to be activated because the surgery site is still too swollen.  I am looking for methods to reduce the swelling in order for her to get activated.
Answer: There are a couple ways to do this, but they won't be cure-alls; just helps.  

Ibuprofen (Advil) is an NSAID, or a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug.  As the description says, it has anti-inflammatory (anti-swelling) properties, and it will help with pain.  More than likely, any other meds you are giving her do not contain ibuprofen or aspirin, but if they do, I wouldn't use this.

Benadryl (Diphenhydramine) has properties which stop the body from reacting to irritants; that's why they use it for rashes, poison ivy, etc.  This would help as well, although it'll probably make her tired.  Diphenhydramine is the exact same drug used in the sleep aid Sominex.  (Yeah, Benadryl and Sominex are the same drug - rip off, eh?  Buy whichever is cheaper...actually, buy the cheap-o generics if they're available -- there really is no difference whatsoever.)

That's about all I can think of over the counter.  Other people may have good ideas as well, and I'd trust the advice of your doctor over anything you read on here.

I'd use coldpacks, but I'd stay away from using heat; it dilates the blood vessels and may make the pain worse.  Heat is best for muscular pain.

P.S. - Her age matters, too.  If we're talking about an infant here, I would go ONLY by the advice of your doctor.

label: Science & Mathematics
sentence:
Title: pathway of taste perception?
Question: Kindly answer this bcus i need it 2morrow....\nIt's all about the Taste Organ..
Answer: The sense of taste of course begins with the taste buds located primarily on the tongue, but also on the soft palate, cheeks, pharynx, and epiglottis.  Chemicals in food stimulate sensory neurons in the taste buds, which communicate with the brain via one of three cranial nerves: the facial nerve (VII), the glossopharyngeal nerve (IX), or the vagus nerve (X).  These nerves enter the central nervous system at the level of the brainstem, synapsing with secondary neurons in the solitary nucleus.  The signals then pass upwards through the thalamus to the gustatory cortex, which is part of the primary somatosensory cortex located on the surface of the parietal lobes.  Note that the functioning of this pathway depends heavily on normal functioning of the sense of smell.  This is why your food tastes bland when you have a bad cold with a stuffy nose.

2.)The slope of the line 3y = x - 3 is
Answer: We can use the point-slope form of the equation and then transform it into the slope-intercept form.

(y - y1) = m(x - x1)
(y - 2) = 4/3(x - 3)
y - 2 = (4/3)x - 4
y  =(4/3)x - 2.

m = 4/3, b = -2

3y = x - 3
y = (1/3)x - 1

The slope m = 1/3

Title: pacemakers?
Question: well my dad's a little older than the average 14 year old's. [[try 79 years old]] and he could possibly need a pacemaker. he's suffered from heart failure, and smoked about 50 years of his life. the way my mom described a pacemaker thing she said they have a procedure to put something on his heart to make it beat better. is this what it is? and could it possibly hurt my dad??? are there any dangers in a pacemaker??\n\ni'm really nervous and don't know what to think...
Answer: well let me assure you it wouldn't hurt him except the surgery. i am 22 and have had 2 pacer (my nickname for pacemaker) surgeies coming up on my third. and while i am very tired and hurting after the surgery, i live a normal life after the healing. now i am not saying you dad will be fine it sounds like he is kinda not healthy with the smoking and all but the pacer won't hurt the situation it'll help. he might be even better after the surgery, more active and stuff, better chance at living longer. the surgey (for most are outpatient which means you pretty much get to go home in the same day) goes like this there is a small disk about the thickness of a cd case slightly bigger maybe 1 and 1/2 cd cases. and round about the size of the top of a pop can. it has two leads (two covered wires) that came out of the disk. they have a small screw on the end of each lead which are screwed into the heart, no worries that doesn't hurt. once the leads are in place chances are they will be there forever they don't go bad and are detachable at the disk end for repacemant surgies. which depends on how much his heart uses it. i use mine 100% of the time and i get about six years out of mine. they put the disk in your shoulder (mines' on the left), or sometimes older ppl have a bag with the disk in it but i think that's for ppl even older. then if they put it in your shoulder they sew you up and leave a scar about two inches wide, and not even an inch thick. the pacer from day one will shock his heart into working kinda similar to the paddles in the er but not quite. it doesn't hurt and you don't even notice it most the time. the only time i feel mine is right before i go to sleep if i hold real still i can feel a slight bump  from the inside but it doesn't hurt i think it's kinda cool and i usually laugh just a little at the thought of what it just was. sometimes i forget i have a pacer and other then being wary of big magnets (which shut off pacers) and playing football (a hard knock to the pacer could possably dislodge the leads) i live a full and happy life. without it i couldn't be here. so your dad has a great chance of being just fine. just be there for him and don't bump his shoulder for at least awhile it does hurt, just like any stiches would. praying wouldn't hurt and don't worry the pacer won't hurt him.

Pluto (IPA: /ˈpluːtəʊ/), designated (134340) Pluto in the Minor Planet Center catalogue, is the second-largest known dwarf planet in the solar system. It orbits between 29 and 49 AU from the Sun, and was the first Kuiper Belt Object to be discovered. Approximately one-fifth the mass of the Earth's Moon, Pluto is primarily composed of rock and ice. It has an eccentric orbit that is highly inclined with respect to the planets and takes it closer to the Sun than Neptune during a portion of its orbit. Pluto and its largest satellite, Charon, could be considered a binary system because they are closer in size than any of the other known planetoid/moon combinations in the solar system, and because the barycentre of their orbits does not lie within either body. However, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) has yet to formalize a definition for binary dwarf planets, so Charon is regarded as a moon of Pluto. Two smaller moons, Nix and Hydra, were discovered in 2005. Pluto is smaller than several of the natural satellites or moons in our solar system (see the list of solar system objects by radius).

From its discovery by Clyde Tombaugh in 1930, Pluto was considered the ninth planet from the Sun. In the late 20th and early 21st century, many similar objects were discovered in the outer solar system, most notably the Trans-Neptunian object Eris which is slightly larger than Pluto. In August 2006 the IAU redefined the term "planet", and classified Pluto, Ceres, and Eris as dwarf planets.[1] Pluto is also classified as the prototype of a family of trans-Neptunian objects.[2][3] After the reclassification, Pluto was added to the list of minor planets and given the number 134340.[4][5]

Title: Were the oldest hominid fossils found in Ethiopia or East Africa?
Question: If so why do people deny have some African ancestry..
Answer: Man originated from earlier primates in eastern Africa. The big step in their evolution is the drying of eastern Africa about 4 million years ago. When the jungles died and separated, what would become man developed a locking knee joint. This enabled them to walk much farther (and endurance run) to cover more ground and obtain more resources, putting them at a distinct advantage to other primates. If you don't believe me, try walking around without locking your knee, it's hard and taxing.

This adaptation allowed for the development of many other things that we've come to love: our large heads and brains (when we were strictly bipedal, we free up our hands for projects, and this favors big brains), short rib cage (for flexibility), and big butts (something has to give you balance when you don't have a tail).

This climate change occurred when New Guinea moved in the way of a prominent current that brought warm, moist water to east Africa. Over time, these newly smart, adapted primates radiated out of Africa and to the rest of the world. See links below for more info.

sentence:
Title: Is Pete Hautman's book, Invisible worth while reading?
Question: Could you give me a basic overview of the book and also tell me what you thought of it.  I have a choice to read it for extra credit, should I?
Answer: Reviews and Commentary
(http://www.petehautman.com/invisibleinfo.html)  

LIBRARY JOURNAL (starred review) 

Seventeen-year-old Dougie takes everything literally, lacks social graces and is a loner, except, perhaps, for his one friend, athletic and popular Andy Morrow. But readers know almost immediately that something tragic has happened in the recent past: ' Andy and I had some bad luck with fires when we were kids. We're more careful now.' Other students feel threatened by Dougie's disturbing behavior and react by targeting him with cruelty and violence, which only serves to escalate his descent into unreality, isolation, and obsession. The teen has been working for nearly three years on his model railroad set, using 22, 400 headless matches to build a bridge connecting portions of the 'Madham Line.' As his life deteriorates, this obsession and his nightly talks with Andy are the only things that keep him clinging to normalcy. He resists the help of his psychiatrist and hides his medication. Ultimately, he is forced to remember what actually happened on that fateful night. With its excellent plot development and unforgettable, heartbreaking protagonist, this is a compelling novel of mental illness. 

  

HORN BOOK (starred review) 

Gifted in math, and recognizably clever when constructing architectural models (he's building an elaborate railroad system in his basement), Doug reveals that it's human interaction he can't figure out. "I'm a quiet kid, pretty much invisible," he says in a precise, unemotional voice, as this unreliable narrator begins his story. Invisibility is Doug's rationale for explaining a range of rejection, from teacher irritation to peer scorn, particularly from pretty and popular Melissa Haverman, who is disgusted by what readers will recognize as Doug's stalker behavior. But Doug reports one near-perfect relationship, the one he has with his best friend, Andy. Gradually, however, that friendship is revealed to be not what it seems. There are secrets from their past that Doug won't discuss, and hints from their present life that skew his tale. Why is there a strange man in Andy's house? What fuels Doug's increasingly complex rendering of their intertwined initials? What medication is Doug refusing to take? Reading this psychological thriller is much like putting together one of Doug's railroad bridges: connections are being made, but the realities being built may be imitations of life rather than the real thing. The tension comes from entering Doug's private hell and learning what put him there. 

  

PUBLISHERS WEEKLY (starred review) 

The strength of Hautman's painfully sad novel is the wisecracking but clearly unreliable voice of its narrator, 17-year-old Douglas MacArthur Hanson who admits, "I'm not only disturbed, I'm obsessed." One of his passions is "Madham," a town he's building for his model railroad, complete with a 1:800 scale replica of the Golden Gate Bridge. He's also fixated on a pretty girl who clearly wants nothing to do with him. And he's overly reliant on his only friend, Andy Morrow, a fellow junior who is the popular and outgoing yang to Dougie's outcast and introverted yin. Hautman expertly teases out the truth about a tragic incident that occurred "at the Tuttle place" three years earlier, a mystery that propels the story to its horrific conclusion. Dougie is as mathematically gifted and socially inept as the autistic narrator of Mark Haddon's The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time, but he also has a sophisticated wit. During a lapse in conversation at one of his $95-an-hour therapy sessions, he observes, "We stare at each other for about $1.40." Title: What are my rights as a leaseholder while property is on the market?
Question: I am leasing an upscale condo in Orange County CA. My rent is 1800./month. I moved in in August 2005 and signed a one year lease. In February, 2006, the owners put it on the market.

What are my rights AND responsibilities in terms of making this home available to prospective buyers?

So far, I have allowed showings without appointments three days a week within certain hours.

I will be working from home for the summer, and cannot work with the threat of the doorbell ringing at any time. I have requested "by appointment only" and am getting significant flak from the listing agent.

My lease is up 7/31 at which point I'll be moving, but I need some advice for getting through the summer -- and to know whether if this all becomes to much, if I have the right to say "ENOUGH." DO I HAVE TO LET PROSPECTIVE BUYERS IN THIS HOUSE, BY CA LAW? I need some advice as I have had no luck reading and interpreting CA code. Thanks.
Answer: The sale of the house has NO affect on your lease.  The buyer takes the house subject to the lease.

The lease should say something about the landlord's right to enter the premises.  While a showing is a valid purpose most states require advanced notice of intent to enter in writing.  There are also legal restrictions on the time of day i.e. not too early in the morning of after dinner at night.  The landlord's entry without advance notice is a lease violation.  You may be entitled to stop paying rent or terminate your tenancy as a result.

The bottom line is that you two are going to have to work it out.  If you are hostile during the showings the house will never sell, and thus the showings will never stop.

Title: For college professors!!!!  Be honest!!?
Question: How do you feel when students leave your class early or don't come at all?  I've been doing this in some of my classes but I don't know if my teachers are offended or if they will not pass me b/c of this.  Thanks for your input!!!!
Answer: I have my attendance policy written on all of my syllabi.   Most of my colleagues do as well.  Usually, there are consequences for missing more than three classes, but these consequences vary from professor to professor.  In my classes, grades begin to drop after three unexcused absences.

However, some professors run their classes in such a way that absences do not impact students' grades.  Professors who have classes like this usually believe that it is a student's responsibility to engage with the material, and if they do not, it is the student's loss, and not the professor's concern.

Every professor I know believes that it is rude and disruptive when students leave class early.   Although I've never failed a student for this, my attitude toward them is certainly affected by their disrespectful behavior.   I'd be much less likely to extend myself to help, or to accept the excuses of a student who regularly demonstrates that they do not respect my life's work.  

When students need to leave class early for important appointments (medical or otherwise), or will be missing a class for specific reasons, they usually contact me beforehand and let me know.  When they demonstrate both good manners and a sense of adult responsibility by doing this, I am completely understanding, and am not at all offended.

Question: What really distinguishes AJAX programming from traditional web programming (html/javascript)?
Answer: AJAX uses a bit of javascript that uses the XmlHTTP object.  This object, opens up a connection to a Web server, transmits and receives data, then calls back the javascript on the page which was used to invoke it.

What this means is that changes on the client side can communicate with the server, then dynamically update the client user interface without having to request a new Web page from the server.

While this slightly complicates developing Web applications that use AJAX technologies (which, by the way, is just a name given to the various technologies employed to use this methodology), it makes for a very smooth user experience since they are not constantly refreshing Web pages.

AJAX applications give an appearance of a 'thick client' application while still being a 'thin client' (i.e. application that runs in a Web browser.)  However, it is important to note that network communication is still going on in the background while the application is being used.

sentence:
Title: Oxalic acid's comp. is 26.7%C,2.2%H,71.1%O. its molecular weight is 90amu. What is its molecular formula?
Question: Oxalic acid is a toxic substance used by laundries to remove rust stains.  Its composition is 26.7% C, 2.2% H, and 71.1% O (by mass), and its molecular weight is 90amu.  What is its molecular formula?
Answer: Call it (CxHyOz)
Mass of C = 12x
Mass of H = 2y
Mass of O = 16z
-----------------------
Its molecular weight M = 12x + 2y + 16z = 90

Percentage of C: (12x / M) *100% = 26.7% <-> 12x = 90 * 26.7 / 100 <-> 12x = 24 <-> x = 2

You can do the same with H and O to find y = 2 and z = 4.

The formula is, hence, C2H2O4.

Answer: In terms of practical differences you can notice today, Chinese have always had top-down governments with no democracy. In China or Taiwan, if it's unclear whether you are allowed to do something or not, the assumption is, you are NOT allowed. Title: Please tell me the best way to show a High School Boys Basketball star to college coaches for a scholarship.?
Question: 16 year old high school junior plays point guard at Lemoore High School.  Lemoore, California.  Lemoore has highest ratio of made 3 point shots in central section, Alex has highest ratio at Lemoore High School.  5'9" 160lbs.  3.5gpa
Answer: Believe it or not, the coaches usually come to you -- early.  I know a 15-year-old, 6'3" high school basketball star who started receiving letters from universities as a freshman.  This was before he was invited to join the varsity basketball team as a freshman.  In short, Big Ten university coaches have been courting him and his parents since he was 14.

Since your star has not been approached at this point, you must take matter into your own hands.  Despite the height factor, treat your star like a product.  Become your own Arliss or Jerry Maguire, i.e., sports agent.  Look at the college sports pages for top twenty lists to map out your target schools.  Assemble a media kit with the newspaper clippings, high school transcripts, a personal essay, letters of recommendation from faculty and community leaders, and action photographs of your star.  Pitch your star to the head coach and assistant coaches.  If they require more information, offer to send them a media kit.  Request an interview.  If possible try to bring your star to meet the coach if his/her team is playing at a nearby university.  Send a thank you note.

If that does not work, network, network, network ... Cultivate relationships with the sports writers at your local and big city newspapers and the sports anchors of your local television networks.  Ask for help.  Then ask for recommendations.  For the most part, if your star is not on the front page of the sports section, then you must be aggressive in gaining coverage.  

Additional keys to boosting the profile of your star are park districts, regional tournaments, traveling teams, basketball festivals, and summer camps.  The more people know about the talents of your star, the better.  It may sound overwhelming (and expensive), but practice and multiple performance venues make perfect public relations for budding NCAA stars.  If your star has not been playing basketball year-round, since kintergarten, then expedite your media campaign -- yesterday.

If your star is really a star, then a scholarship is in your reach.  So, roll up your sleeves and claim it.  Ask the basketball coach, athletic director, principal and teachers for support in your endeavor because the universities will confirm your information.

Again, year-round participation is of vital importance.  So, research leagues outside of high school.

Have a grateful day.

Question: What Is Correlation and Cross Correlation?
Answer: Correlation is determining the relationship of one variable to the values of other variables using collected data.

For example if you considered a person's salary, you might find it correlates with: number of years of education, and number of years of employment, along with other variables.

Cross-correlation means a correlation just between 2 variables. You get that expression, because you can evaluate if two variables cross correlate, by plotting one variable on the X and one on the Y axis of a graph. If the cloud of points that result are clustered around a straight line then they cross correlate well.

Question: How do you account for the smell of vinegar when an old bottle of aspirin is opened.?
Answer: The acetyl salicylic acid undergoes ester hydrolysis on long term standing to produce acetic acid (vinegar) and salicylic acid.  The problem was that salicylic acid was tough on stomachs and a means of 'buffering' the compound was searched for. The first person to do so was a French chemist named Charles Frederic Gerhardt. In 1853, Gerhardt neutralized salicylic acid by buffering it with sodium (sodium salicylate) and acetyl chloride, creating acetylsalicylic acid. Gerhardt's product worked but he had no desire to market it and abandoned his discovery. 

In 1899, a German chemist named Felix Hoffmann, who worked for a German company called Bayer, rediscovered Gerhardt's formula. Felix Hoffmann made some of the formula and gave it to his father who was suffering from the pain of arthritis. With good results, Felix Hoffmann then convinced Bayer to market the new wonder drug. Aspirin was patented on March 6, 1889. 

The folks at Bayer came up with the name Aspirin, it comes from the 'A" in acetyl chloride, the "spir" in spiraea ulmaria (the plant they derived the salicylic acid from) and the 'in' was a then familiar name ending for medicines. 

Aspirin was first sold as a powder. In 1915, the first Aspirin tablets were made. Interestingly, Aspirin ® and Heroin ® were once trademarks belonging to Bayer. After Germany lost World War I, Bayer was forced to give up both trademarks as part of the Treaty of Versailles in 1919.

Title: Had anyone ever heard the legend of the Hornet Spooklight?
Question: I've heard lots of different legends, the most famous one being the legend of the Hornet Spooklight, somewhere near Joplin, Missouri. Does anyone know more about it, and know where I can find more information about it?
Answer: The Spooklight, also called the Hornet Spooklight or Devil's Promenade, is a mysterious visual phenomenon allegedly experienced by witnesses in a small area known locally as the "Devil's Promenade" on the border between southwestern Missouri and northeastern Oklahoma west of the small town of Hornet, Missouri. Despite the fact that it is named after a small, unincorporated community in Missouri from which it is most commonly accessed, the light is most commonly described as being visible from inside the Oklahoma border looking to the west. The Spooklight is commonly described as a single ball of light or a tight grouping of lights that is said to appear in the area regularly, usually at night. Although the description of the light is similar to that of other visual phenomena witnessed throughout the world, the term "Spooklight" when standing alone generally refers to this specific case. Numerous legends exist that attempt to desribe the origin of the Spooklight, one of which involves the ghosts of two young Native American lovers looking for each other.\n\nAccording to most accounts, it has appeared continually since the late 19th Century, although it was generally not well-known to anyone but locals until after World War II. Some date the first encounters with the light back to the Trail of Tears in the 1830s. However, the first documented sighting is generally accepted to have occurred in 1881, although some report sightings as far back as 1866. The earliest published report dates back to 1936 in the Kansas City Star. In 1946 the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers supposedly studied the "Hornet Light", but could not find a cause for it. In their words, it was a "mysterious light of unknown origin". Early residents of the area reported seeing lights in the forest, over their land, or even in their yards. During the 1960s, there was a general store in Hornet that gave out information about the light to sightseers. It included a "Spooklight museum". There have also been various establishments along the Missouri-Oklahoma state line that served a similar function, but they have since closed. During the 1960s and 1970s the roads where the Spooklight usually appears were often packed with parked vehicles and people hoping to get a glimpse of the mysterious light.-

Title: Mt Etna eruption 1999?
Question: What Strategies came into place after the event?
Answer: Mt. Etna's eruptions, while obscuring visibility in the area surrounding the volcano, were captured by cameras on board the Terra and SeaWiFs satellites in recent days.

The eruption opened six vents in the mountain, releasing a cloud of ash stretching southeastward over the Mediterranean Sea, though the volatile mountain's lava flows have appeared to slowed.

A new fissure cracked open at a height of 2,700 yards (2,470 meters) on the eastern side of the volcano, officials told Reuters on Tuesday, weakening the main lava flow that threatened the village of Nicolosi, a community of 5,000 people. 

The magma pouring out of the new fissure, one of a half-dozen that have burst open on the almost 11,000-foot (3,350-meter) mountain, was heading toward the uninhabited Valle del Bove valley. 

"There are very slight signals that the eruption activity is diminishing. I am cautiously optimistic,'' said Alberto Di Pace, prefect of Catania, a city at the base of the volcano. 

But experts say the volcano is highly unpredictable, making it extremely difficult to tell whether the eruptions will stop soon. In the past 20 days there have been more than 2,500 tremors under the mountain, with no signs of any let-up. 

Catania's international airport, which was shut for a second time on Monday as thick layers of volcanic ash covered the runway, was re-opened at 6:00 a.m. on Tuesday. 

For a week, Europe's most active volcano has been billowing huge clouds of smoke and black ash, and spitting rivers of lava, leading the government to declare a state of emergency. 

The lava flow approaching Nicolosi has almost stopped as it pools in a shallow basin some 2.5 miles above the village. 

On Sunday, the community organized a religious procession to pray that the flow be diverted or stopped. 

Legend has it that in 1886 the local archbishop managed to divert a wave of boiling magma descending on the village by brandishing before it a statue of Saint Anthony. 

The magma has already damaged ski lifts dotting the volcano's slopes and civil protection teams were trying to save the ones left intact. 

Mount Etna is a popular winter resort, but tourism officials say snow is unlikely to settle this winter because of the extreme heat of the lava. 

The last time Etna posed a threat was in 1992 when lava streams headed toward Zafferana, a town of 7,000 people on Etna's lower slopes. The Italian military had to use controlled explosions to divert the flow.

label: Health
sentence:
Question: What is emphysema and what are its causes?
Answer: Q. What is Emphysema?
FAQ

From Stacey Lloyd,
Your Guide to Lung Diseases.

A.

Emphysema is a lung disease in which the walls of the alveoli (air sacs) in the lungs fracture or burst. As these alveoli break, the remaining alveoli become enlarged to make up for the loss. This results in a fewer number of alveoli, with many enlarged. 
When alveoli are enlarged, they loose their elasticity. A loss of elasticity in the alveoli results in the inability to eliminate air from the lungs. Therefore, patients must use force (energy) to expel this air. 

Furthermore, the loss of elasticity in the lungs affects the smaller bronchial tubes. To push air out of the bronchial tubes, a higher pressure must be developed inside the chest. 

This higher pressure tends to collapse the smaller bronchial tubes, making it even more difficult to empty air from the alveoli. 
Coughing becomes very difficult and ineffective in expelling mucus, leaving the lungs more susceptible to lung infections, such as pneumonia. 

( http://lungdiseases.about.com/od/emphysema/f/emphysema_expl.htm )

What causes emphysema?
Emphysema can be caused by one or a combination of these things:

Cigarette smoking: Most cases of emphsyema are caused by cigarette smoking. Cigarette smoke reaches deep into the lungs and causes permanent damage. If you have emphysema from cigarettes, the best way to stop your lung damage is to quit smoking as soon as possible. It's never too late to quit smoking. 
Alpha-1 Antitrypsin deficiency: Some people have emphsyema because of a rare genetic disorder called Alpha-1 Antitrypsin deficiency. People with Alpha-1 are missing an enzyme that protects their lungs. Some people with Alpha-1 deficiency get emphysema without ever having smoked. Other people get emphsyema from the combination of smoking and having Alpha-1 deficiency. 
Air pollution: There is some evidence that air pollution can contribute to people getting emphysema, especially if the person also smokes. ( http://www.lung.ca/diseases-maladies/a-z/emphysema-emphyseme/index_e.php#causes )

Title: Does anyone have a successful instant credit program idea?
Question: I am a manager for a retail chain that allows customers to open up lines of credit instantly at our checkouts. We have entered a dull season (the time between Labor Day and Back To School) and our instant credit performance is slipping, even though we have offered a high-ticket item as incentive. Does anyone have any successful ideas for employee motivation, pitch ideas or anything that can help raise our numbers back to goal?
Answer: You never want to give away gifts in exchange for a credit sign-up - as a rule of thumb, financial programs are poorly sold when a financial incentive is provided up front.  Your target audience are individuals who desire to make a purchase but may be hesitating due to lack of funds and credit.  So go to the highest priced items in your store, and have signs that say, "$100 for this TV, but if you sign up for a credit card today, you only pay $12 per month in payments" etc.  Market the card next to your highest price gifts to drive adoption of the credit program.  In fact, have credit apps next to these areas, so they don't forget to sign up on the back to the front of the store.

Title: Who discovered irregular galaxies?
Question: or Any other info about irregular galaxies
Answer: Pierre Méchain

Irregular galaxies are those which do not match the standard Hubble scheme of elliptical, spiral and lenticular galaxies. 
There's only one irregular galaxy in Messier's catalog: M82, and this one is a distorted disk galaxy. The distortion is due to gravitational interaction with its larger and more massive neighbor M81. 

Another, very similar example is at least mentioned in Messier's catalog, though it did not get a number on its own: NGC 5195, the companion of the Whirlpool galaxy M51, which had been discovered by Pierre Méchain. The only further irregular galaxies known to 1782 are the Large and the Small Magellanic Cloud; these are probably miniature disk galaxies in mutual gravitational interaction, and in interaction with our Milky Way.

Title: What will happen?
Question: what will happen if imagine we could dig a tunnel from one side of the earth and came out through another and then drop a stone into it. Will it come out through the other side? What will be the result?
Answer: Ignoring the following things: the rotation of the earth, and the fact that the earth is not solid all the way through...

If you drilled a hole all the way through and dropped a stone in, it would accelerate until it got to the center of the earh, then it would start to decelerate.  It would ALMOST make it to the other side.  The reason it wouldn't make it all the way is because some of its kinetic energy was lost to friction with the air in the hole.  After it got as far as it could go, it would start to come back, and it would travel even less distance before starting to "fall" again.  Each time it would lose a little more energy until it eventually would come to rest at the center of the earth.  And note that the stone wouldn't be resting ON anything, it would just be at rest, in "mid-air", if you like.  

If you want to go one step further and ignore friction, the stone WOULD make it to the other side, but just barely.  If no one were there to catch it, then it would just oscillate back and forth forever, from the point where you dropped it to its antipodal* counterpart.
This would make a good method of travel, no?  Just hop in the hole, and in a little while you'd pop out the other side of the earth, as if you'd just teleported or something (of course this is a non- physical scenario). 

*vocab:
antipodal points = opposite points on a sphere
